papers.abstract: Designing catalysts that maximize both atomic efficiency and catalytic activity remains a central challenge in heterogeneous catalysis. While single-atom catalysts maximize noble metal utilization, their isolated structure limits the adsorption configurations of adsorbates, thereby diminishing their catalytic efficiency. We present a versatile platform based on atom-layer neighbors, where the proximity of Ru ensembles diversifies adsorption configurations while simultaneously enhancing adsorbate binding through ligand effects. By leveraging molecular interactions and strong metal-support interactions, we thermodynamically stabilize atomically thin structures comprising only a few Ru atoms, allowing the synthesis of size-tuned Ru atom-layer neighbors on WCx supports. The optimized *H binding on size-tuned Ru ensembles, combined with *OH enrichment on WCx supports, leads to competitive activity per unit noble metal cost in anion-exchange membrane water electrolyzers. Notably, our catalyst achieves the DOE 2026 performance target for PEMWE even at a lower temperature of 60 °C, with a Ru loading of 0.100 mg cm-2, below the DOE's ultimate noble metal loading threshold. This atom-layer neighbor platform offers a general strategy for enhancing catalyst efficiency while maintaining high noble metal utilization.

papers.abstract: Abstract Background It is unclear whether glioma subtypes differ in health-related quality of life (HRQoL) over time. Methods We analyzed data from the CODAGLIO 2.0 database, comprising 16 randomized controlled trials with HRQoL assessed using the EORTC QLQ-C30 and QLQ-BN20 questionnaires. Differences in mean HRQoL at baseline (before postoperative treatments) and 3 months were compared across glioma subtypes. Linear mixed models (LMMs) were used to identify factors independently associated with HRQoL, and anchor-based minimally important differences determined clinical relevance. Results A total of 4,301 patients had baseline HRQoL data; 75% completed follow-up. In stratified analyses, at 3 months, physical, social, role, and cognitive functioning were statistically and clinically significantly worse in glioblastoma than in astrocytoma or oligodendroglioma. In adjusted LMMs, compared with glioblastoma, patients with astrocytoma had worse physical (−2.78, 95% CI, −4.68 to −1.01) and cognitive functioning (−3.63, −6.18 to −1.05), more pain (2.74, 0.41-4.95), communication deficits (5.03, 2.44-7.66), and seizures (4.49, 2.55-6.72). Patients with oligodendroglioma had worse social functioning (−5.39, −10.57 to −0.11), communication deficits (7.40, 1.63-12.81), and seizures (8.61, 4.17-14.26). None of these differences exceeded clinical relevance thresholds. Performance status was the only variable associated with clinically meaningful HRQoL changes across most scales. Conclusions At 3 months, patients with glioblastoma show clinically worse HRQoL than IDH-mutant glioma patients in unadjusted analyses. However, after adjusting for clinical variables, glioblastoma patients exhibit statistically but not clinically better HRQoL in several domains. Performance status emerges as the key factor independently associated with HRQoL and should play a central role in clinical decision-making.

papers.abstract: Cervical cancer is a common malignancy in women worldwide, with distant metastases frequently occurring in the lungs, liver, bones, and lymph nodes. However, this case report presents an extremely rare isolated metastasis to the left scapular region,specifically located between the supraspinatus and the trapezius muscles, in a patient with locally advanced cervical squamous cell carcinoma who developed this lesion during maintenance therapy with a programmed death receptor-1 (PD-1) inhibitor after completing concurrent chemoradiotherapy. The clinical presentation of this metastatic lesion was atypical and posed a significant diagnostic challenge; however, multimodal imaging (MRI, PET/CT) and histopathological examination ultimately confirmed the diagnosis of cervical cancer metastasis. This finding underscores the necessity of maintaining a high level of vigilance for metastases in atypical sites, even in the era of immunotherapy. To manage this rare presentation, a multidisciplinary team developed a comprehensive treatment strategy centered on surgical resection, followed by postoperative adjuvant radiotherapy administered concurrently with chemotherapy and anti-angiogenic therapy(Q3W) consisting of paclitaxel 135 mg/m², cisplatin 50 mg/m², and bevacizumab 10 mg/kg. The patient remained recurrence-free at 13 months, suggesting that a multimodal combined local and systemic strategy may be feasible for selected patients with solitary muscle metastasis. This case not only adds to the clinical understanding of rare metastases in cervical cancer but also demonstrates that tumors can still metastasize to atypical sites under immunotherapy. These findings highlight the need for vigilance regarding metastases at atypical sites during immunotherapy. Any underlying mechanism-including immune editing and clonal evolution-remains speculative in the absence of paired molecular data and requires further validation.

papers.abstract: To compare overall survival (OS) in patients with relapsed neuroblastoma treated with dinutuximab beta (DB) after relapse with that of two comparator populations: historical controls with no prior anti-disialoganglioside-2 exposure and patients who relapsed after first-line DB maintenance immunotherapy. The objectives were to evaluate the effectiveness of DB in the relapsed setting and to assess a potential legacy effect of prior first-line therapy. This unanchored indirect comparison used individual patient data from three cohorts: historical controls with no prior anti-GD2 therapy (N/N), patients who relapsed after first-line DB maintenance immunotherapy and did not receive subsequent DB (DB/N), and patients treated with DB after relapse without prior exposure (N/DB). Harmonized eligibility criteria were applied across cohorts, and follow-up was aligned using a common post-relapse index date. Adjusted comparisons were performed using propensity score reweighting. Overall survival was measured from the observed (N/DB) or imputed (N/N and DB/N) post-relapse index date and analyzed using weighted Kaplan-Meier methods and weighted Cox proportional hazards models, with hazard ratios (HR) reported. For the N/N and DB/N cohorts, the post-relapse index date was imputed using a quantile regression model estimating the interval from first relapse to initiation of DB, fitted to data from the N/DB cohort. A total of 329 patients were assessed, of whom 266 were included in the weighted analyses. Baseline imbalances in age at relapse, time from diagnosis, MYCN status, and International Neuroblastoma Staging System (INSS) stage were largely resolved after weighting. No evidence of a legacy effect of first-line DB exposure was observed, as OS did not differ significantly between patients who relapsed after first-line DB maintenance immunotherapy and historical controls (HR = 1.26, 95% CI 0.70-2.26; p=0.437). In contrast, DB administered after relapse was associated with significantly improved OS compared with both historical controls (HR = 0.53, 95% CI 0.35-0.81; p=0.003) and patients who relapsed after first-line DB maintenance immunotherapy (HR = 0.42, 95% CI 0.25-0.72; p=0.001). These findings were consistent across sensitivity analyses. This adjusted indirect comparison demonstrated that DB administered after relapse was associated with significantly improved OS compared with both historical controls and patients who relapsed after prior first-line DB maintenance immunotherapy. No evidence of a legacy effect of first-line DB immunotherapy was identified. These findings support the clinical relevance of DB in the relapsed setting and indicate that prior first-line DB maintenance alone was not associated with a persistent post-relapse survival advantage. The study did not evaluate DB retreatment after prior first-line exposure.

papers.abstract: The 2026 American Society of Clinical Oncology (ASCO) Annual Meeting presented substantial new data on antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) in lung cancer, highlighting the ongoing expansion of ADC-based strategies from later-line treatment toward first-line combination regimens. This focused narrative review summarizes and discusses the efficacy and safety findings of ADCs targeting TROP2, HER2, Nectin-4, PD-L1, c-Met, B7-H3, DLL3, SEZ6, and other emerging targets in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and small cell lung cancer (SCLC), with particular attention to emerging ADC plus immune checkpoint inhibitor combinations in the first-line setting. Taken together, these findings highlight an expanding ADC landscape in lung cancer. However, many of the emerging strategies remain supported primarily by preliminary conference-reported or early-phase data and therefore require confirmation in mature peer-reviewed studies and adequately powered randomized clinical trials.

In the past 40 years, enormous progress has been achieved in the clinical and basic research on H. pylori infection. However, challenges in preventing and treating H. pylori infection exist owing to the lack of an H. pylori vaccine and the ever-increasing resistance to antibiotics worldwide. This review summarizes the history of and key milestones in H. pylori research, provides an update on the understanding of the pathogenesis and global burden of H. pylori infection and the screening strategy for the primary prevention of gastric cancer, and focuses on the emerging trends in the management of H. pylori infection.

papers.abstract: Prediction of CRISPR/Cas outcomes remains unsatisfactory in embryos due to distinct DNA repair preferences and the lack of large-scale embryo editing profiles. We introduce inDecay, a flexible system for predicting the proportion of CRISPR-induced indels from the target sequence. Owing to its parameter-efficient and cell-type-aware design, inDecay performs well in both in-sample training and out-of-sample fine-tuning. Starting with cross-cell-line predictions, we observed that inDecay maintains high accuracy in mouse zygote editing and in goat, cattle and porcine embryos. inDecay may accelerate mouse model generation, livestock embryonic editing, and gene therapy applications.

papers.abstract: Vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecium (VREfm) is a major cause of hospital-associated infections globally. In the Capital Region of Denmark, VREfm ST80 emerged as the dominant vanA-positive clone but declined significantly over the following decade. To investigate the genomic mechanisms underlying this epidemiological shift, we assembled and performed whole-genome sequencing and phylogenomic analysis of 334 ST80 isolates collected from colonisation (83%) and infection (17%) cases across nine hospitals in the region between 2012 and 2020. Two major clusters (Clusters 1 and 2) and nine sub-clusters (1.A-G and 2.H-I) were identified. Sub-cluster-1.A (169/334) was the dominant lineage, accounting for 72% of isolates from 2012-2015. Isolates from 2016-2020 were distributed across all sub-clusters, indicating increasing diversification over time. Genetic variation was driven by accumulation of mutations, recombination and gain/loss of accessory genes and plasmids. Eight recombination hotspots were identified in core genes involved in cell wall synthesis, phosphotransferase systems, amino-acid biosynthesis, and several transporters. Accessory genome comparisons revealed sub-cluster-specific enrichment of resistance genes, including ermG (89% in 1.B), tet(S) (85% in 1.A), and tet(M) (88% in sub-cluster-1.B). Additionally, genes associated with biofilm formation, ABC transporters, and biosynthesis of polysaccharides, terpenoids, and aspartate were differentially enriched across the clusters. These genomic signatures may have contributed to niche adaptation and intra-clonal diversification. Plasmidome analysis showed increased diversity in later years, with the decline of Inc18 family plasmids (from 80 to 38%) and the rise of two new plasmids, coinciding with reduced clonal stability. Long-read hybrid assemblies uncovered mosaic phage-like plasmids harboring the vanA operon alongside ermB, aadE, and aph(3')-IIIa suggesting a unique mechanism for co-mobilization of antimicrobial resistance via transduction or conjugation. Despite the observed diversity, a continuous and sustained intra- and inter-hospital transmission and dissemination of this clone was evidenced by the small SNP difference (≤ 15 SNPs) between strains. This study showed the continuous hospital transmission and intra-clonal diversity of VREfm ST80. The dissemination, transmission and persistence dynamics of the vanA ST80 clone in Denmark may have been shaped by recombination events and gain/loss of genes involved in general metabolism, antibiotic resistance and virulence, and inter-clonal competition.

papers.abstract: Ovarian cancer (OC) remains highly lethal due to frequent late-stage diagnosis and the challenge of distinguishing malignant from benign adnexal masses (BAM) preoperatively. Reliable non-invasive diagnostic biomarkers remain an unmet clinical need. This multi-center study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic potential of plasma circulating cell-free mitochondrial DNA (ccf-mtDNA) fragmentomics for improving OC management. We developed two machine learning models based on ccf-mtDNA features: an OC Detection (OD) model to distinguishing OC from healthy controls (HC), and a Benign vs. Malignant Differential diagnosis (BMD) model to discriminate OC from BAM. The OD model achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.987 in the training cohort and maintained high performance (AUC above 0.979) in internal and external validation cohorts, with 91.67% sensitivity for Stage I OC at 95% specificity. The BMD model demonstrated strong discriminatory power (AUC = 0.982) and generalizability (AUC ranging from 0.961 to 0.980 in four validation cohorts), significantly outperforming serum biomarkers. Remarkably, both models performed robustly in the Chinese minority cohort. These findings establish ccf-mtDNA fragmentomics as a powerful liquid biopsy approach for the early and accurate detection of OC, with significant potential for clinical translation in high-risk populations and differential diagnosis of benign vs. malignant adnexal masses.

papers.abstract: The E. coli CNF1 toxin hijacks the host laminin 511 receptor, Lu/BCAM, to enter cells. Here, we present the high-resolution cryo-EM structures of full-length CNF1, the CNF1-BCAM complex, and the physiological laminin 511-BCAM complex. Structural analysis uncovers that CNF1 targets the V2 domain of BCAM, mimicking the interaction mode of laminin 511. We demonstrate that CNF1 binds BCAM with higher affinity than laminin 511, effectively displacing the physiological ligand from the cell surface. Leveraging this high-affinity interaction, we engineered a CNF1 D5-based T-cell engager (TCE). This TCE potently directs T cells to kill BCAM-overexpressing tumor cells in vitro and suppresses tumor progression in a metastatic ovarian cancer mouse model in female mice. These findings provide structural insight into how CNF1 hijacks the BCAM receptor and show how a pathogen-derived, high-affinity interaction can be harnessed to redirect T cells against BCAM-expressing tumors.

papers.abstract: Femtosecond laser direct writing enables precise three-dimensional structuring of transparent materials. However, in fluoride glasses-key platforms for mid-infrared photonics-the pathway linking ultrafast energy deposition to permanent refractive-index modification remains mechanistically unclear. Here, we decode this multiscale pathway from femtosecond excitation to microscale structural modification in fluoroindate glass by integrating time-resolved pump-probe shadowgraphy, birefringence imaging, microscopic elemental analysis, and physics-based modelling. Plasma evolution dynamics reveal peak electron densities approaching 5 × 1020 cm-3 at 1.2 ps, accompanied by gigapascal-level stress waves propagating at ~4.3 μm/ns. These transient processes generate steep thermal-pressure gradients that drive ion-selective redistribution, producing polarizability-dependent refractive index changes (Δn ≈ 10-3-10-2). By correlating plasma dynamics, stress evolution, and compositional redistribution, we establish a unified framework linking energy deposition and structural reconfiguration. The results clarify that positive index regions (i.e., regions with a higher refractive index than the unmodified glass matrix) originate from cation densification (Pb/In enrichment), whereas negative regions are associated with outward F/Ba redistribution and reduced local polarizability. This mechanistic insight provides a physically grounded framework for controllable femtosecond laser processing of fluoride glasses and for mechanism-guided design of mid-infrared integrated photonic structures.

papers.abstract: The eicosanoid PGE2 upregulates intracellular Ca²⁺/cAMP levels and induces a cellular immune response, whereas EpOME inhibits PGE2 activity in insects. However, the molecular interactions between the two antagonistic ligands remain largely unexplored. Here we identify nine homologs of vertebrate C18-oxylipin-associating GPCRs among the GPCRs of Spodoptera exigua (SeGPCRs). Functional homology is validated through RNA interference screening, followed by heterologous expressions in both directions between insect and human cell lines. A deletion mutant of SeGPCR48, generated via CRISPR/Cas9, loses responsiveness to EpOME, which is confirmed functionally and by differential gene expression analysis following RNA-seq. In silico binding assay indicate high binding affinity of EpOME to SeGPCR48, which is supported by experimental follow-up, involving ligand-binding functional assays and point mutagenesis of two residues in the binding pocket. In congruence with the in vitro experiments, the EpOME-SeGPCR48 ligand-receptor pair showed marked inhibitory activity against PGE2-mediated immunity. Collectively, this study identifies an insect EpOME receptor within an orphan GPCR subfamily that is phylogenetically conserved across metazoans.

papers.abstract: Phages have evolved various anti-CRISPR (Acr) proteins or RNA-based anti-CRISPR (Racr) to evade host CRISPR immunity by direct interference. However, whether other counter-CRISPR mechanisms exist remains unexplored. Here, we report a phage-encoded two-protein system, termed Healer, which neutralizes CRISPR immunity via a post-cleavage DNA repair mechanism. This phage replication-associated system comprises two proteins: Gp63 (a DUF669 domain-containing protein), and Gp64 (an AAA domain-containing protein). Mechanistic investigations elucidate that Gp63 acts as a rapid-response effector of CRISPR-induced DNA breaks. After Gp63 binds ssDNA, it promotes Gp64-mediated homologous recombination, which repairs CRISPR-generated phage DNA breaks and supports phage viability. Notably, co-expression of the Healer system with Cas9/Cas12 in E. coli, P. aeruginosa, and A. baumannii demonstrated high phage genome-editing efficiency. Collectively, our findings reveal an important anti-CRISPR complementary strategy, providing a promising tool for genome engineering.

papers.abstract: Understanding how tumor cells shape the tumor microenvironment (TME) and evade the host immune response is critical for developing novel therapeutic combinations. In this study, we identify tumor cell p38α as a therapeutic target that restricts antitumor immunity and contributes to resistance against immune-checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). Genetic analyses of mouse and human melanomas reveal alterations in the mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK)-stress pathway, including upregulation of MAPK14. We demonstrate a dual role for p38α in ultraviolet-B (UVB)-induced Braf V600E melanoma, acting as a tumor suppressor during melanocyte transformation but promoting melanoma growth and progression. Mechanistically, p38α impairs cytotoxic immune responses, modulates immunosuppressive myeloid cells, and regulates inflammatory mediators that shape the TME. Loss or inhibition of p38α enhances and restores sensitivity to PD-1 blockade, resulting in tumor regression and improved overall survival. Moreover, a p38α-associated gene signature correlates with favorable immunotherapy outcomes in patients with melanoma, underscoring its translational relevance.

papers.abstract: The gold standard for repair of peripheral nerve injuries is a nerve autograft. Donor nerve harvest creates a second surgical site, invariable numbness and donor site chronic neuropathic pain in 20% of cases. We developed a poly-caprolactone (PCL) multichannel, biomimetic scaffold with surface features promoting cell and vascular attachment and rapid, linear axonal regeneration. The cross-sectional area available for axonal regeneration exceeds that of autografts. When compared to nerve autografts and FDA-approved nerve conduits in 1cm-long rat and 3cm-long rabbit sciatic gap injury, biomimetic scaffolds were equivalent or superior to nerve autografts on measures of axonal regeneration, re-connection between gastrocnemius muscle and spinal cord motor neurons, and evoked motor responses. Scaffolds were superior in all measures to open tube conduits. Biomimetic multichannel scaffolds have potential to replace the need for autografting for peripheral nerve gap repair and are now undergoing multicenter clinical trials.

papers.abstract: Public T cell receptors (TCRs) recurrently emerge across individuals in response to common pathogens, yet the structural and biophysical basis distinguishing public from private clonotypes remains incompletely defined. Here, we combine epitope mapping, single-cell TCR sequencing, and single-particle cryo-electron microscopy to dissect CD8+ T cell responses to the immunodominant SARS-CoV-2 ORF3a(207-215) epitope presented by HLA-A*01:01. Among responding clonotypes, we identify a public TCR (TCRpub), shared across donors, and a private TCR (TCRpriv) that uses nearly identical β chains but distinct α chains. Despite comparable micromolar affinities and functional avidities, cryo-EM structures at ~3 Å resolution reveal that the two receptors engage the peptide-MHC complex through distinct CDR-loop configurations and contact footprints. TCRpub establishes contacts with the peptide and the MHC α2-helix primarily through the CDR2β and CDR3β loops, whereas TCRpriv distributes contacts across both MHC α-helices and engages the peptide via multiple CDR loops. In agreement with these observations, alanine-scanning mutagenesis reveals that TCRpub shows greater sensitivity to peptide substitutions, consistent with its peptide-focused binding mode. These findings demonstrate how alternative α-chain pairing reconfigures the antigen-binding interface within a shared β-chain.

papers.abstract: Protein hydrogels are promising artificial extracellular matrices (ECMs) for 3D stem cell and organoid culture due to their favorable stress relaxation behavior (a decrease in stress in response to strain). Inter-chain entangled motifs, in which different protein chains are interlaced, represent a powerful strategy to synthesize such hydrogels. However, designing these motifs with tailored properties such as binding energy remains a major challenge due to the difficulty of simultaneously controlling these properties while ensuring entanglement. Here, we introduce TangleDiff, a deep learning framework for the de novo design of homodimeric entangled proteins with programmable features. TangleDiff generates diverse foldable entangled sequences with an in-silico success rate exceeding 70%, markedly outperforming current models (~1%). By conditioning TangleDiff on inter-chain binding energy, we generate novel protein dimers whose binding energies closely match the specified ranges, with approximately 70% of successful designs conforming to expected values. We experimentally validate TangleDiff by designing nine homodimers targeting various binding energies; seven successfully form hydrogels, with stress relaxation dynamics correlated with specified binding energies. This work establishes a general strategy for entangled protein design, opening avenues for entanglement-based biomaterial innovation.

papers.abstract: Transposable elements (TEs) are temporally activated during mammalian early embryogenesis and are closely linked to zygotic genome activation (ZGA), yet their nascent transcriptional dynamics remain incompletely resolved owing to limited sensitivity and maternal RNA background. Here, we develop single-cell TimeLapse sequencing (scTL-seq), enabling allele-resolved detection of nascent RNA in individual embryos. Applying scTL-seq to mouse ZGA, we generate a refined transcriptional atlas of genes and TEs and identify the pronuclear (PN) stage activated genes and TEs. We found that transcription at PN stage is largely contributed by the maternal genome and enriched for genes highly transcribed in germinal vesicle oocytes. Similarly, Mouse Transcripts type-A (MTA) elements are transcribed in oocytes and highly active in PN stage. MTA knockdown disrupts zygotic gene activation and dysregulates hundreds of TE subfamilies, resulting in 1-cell embryo arrest. Using nascent transcripts, we further identify 662 TE-driven chimeric transcripts and show that TEs are essential for regulating key developmental genes, including Nfya, Setd2 and Tead4. Finally, we identify maternal transcription factors, including NOBOX, as potential regulators of MTA activation. Together, our study provides a high-resolution nascent transcriptome landscape of mouse ZGA and reveals vital regulatory roles of MTA retrotransposon in orchestrating early embryonic development.

papers.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea, characterized by frequent interruptions in breathing and intermittent hypoxia, is a public health concern due to its potential to increase multiple organ system morbidity and mortality. Although polysomnography is the gold standard for diagnosis, it is laborious, costly, and complex. Here, we present a biological geometry-aware artificial intelligence framework that processes physiological signals to predict sleep apnea severity. This framework extracts multifractal coupling features that capture long-range dependencies among physiological processes and integrates them into deep learning for classification. We validate this approach across five heterogeneous cohorts comprising more than 35,000 subjects. The method achieves robust and consistent performance, with area-under-the-curve values exceeding 0.91 and improvements of 8-18% over state-of-the-art models. The extracted coupling representations exhibit rapid convergence and consistent performance across heterogeneous cohorts. This framework provides a robust representation of physiological dynamics and supports future developments in automated analysis of sleep-disordered breathing.

papers.abstract: Mitophagy is essential for mitochondrial quality control during myocardial ischemia-reperfusion (I/R) injury. Lysosomal protein transmembrane 5 (LAPTM5) has been implicated in cardiovascular disease and autophagy, but its role in cardiac mitophagy remains unclear. LAPTM5 knockout mice and cardiomyocyte-targeted AAV9-cTnT-LAPTM5 were used to determine the role of LAPTM5 in myocardial I/R injury. Cardiomyocyte hypoxia/reoxygenation models, mt-Keima imaging, mitochondrial fractionation, LC3-mitochondrial colocalization, co-immunoprecipitation, molecular docking, site-directed mutagenesis, NEDD4 gain- and loss-of-function, and p62 ubiquitination assays were used to investigate the underlying mechanism. Depending on data distribution and group number, appropriate parametric or non-parametric statistics were applied together with correction for multiple testing. LAPTM5 expression progressively decreased following I/R or H/R stress. LAPTM5 deficiency aggravated myocardial injury, cardiac dysfunction, and mitochondrial structural and functional damage, whereas LAPTM5 overexpression attenuated these abnormalities. LAPTM5 promoted mitophagy by enhancing LC3 recruitment to mitochondria. Mechanistically, LAPTM5 recruited NEDD4 to mitochondria through its PY3 motif and facilitated NEDD4-LC3 complex formation. NEDD4 depletion abolished LAPTM5-mediated mitophagy and cytoprotection, whereas re-expression of NEDD4-WT, but not the E3-inactive NEDD4-CS mutant, restored these effects. NEDD4-WT also increased p62 ubiquitination. AAV9-mediated LAPTM5 re-expression reduced infarct size, improved cardiac function, and preserved mitochondrial integrity in LAPTM5-deficient hearts. LAPTM5 protects against myocardial I/R injury by promoting mitophagy through the NEDD4-LC3 axis. PY3-dependent recruitment of NEDD4 and its E3 ubiquitin ligase activity facilitate LC3-associated mitochondrial clearance, accompanied by enhanced p62 ubiquitination, thereby preserving mitochondrial homeostasis during reperfusion.

papers.abstract: Active surveillance is recommended as the first-line management for desmoid-type fibromatosis (DF); however, data on DF of the head and neck (H&N) and shoulder regions are limited. We examined patients with DF located in the H&N and shoulder regions, comparing baseline characteristics and event-free survival (EFS). A subgroup analysis was performed among patients initially managed with active surveillance. H&N accounted for 4% of all DF cases, and shoulder accounted for 5%. Pain (62% vs. 53% and 33%, respectively; p = 0.01) and functional impairment (29% vs. 0% and 6%, respectively; p = 0.002) were significantly more frequent in shoulder DF compared with H&N DF and DF at other sites. Regardless of initial management, the 3-year EFS rates for H&N and shoulder were similar to those for other locations (p = 0.74). Among patients initially managed with active surveillance, the 3-year EFS rates for H&N and shoulder were similar to that for DF at other locations (p = 0.63). Pain and functional impairment differed significantly by location; however, the outcomes of both H&N and shoulder DF did not differ significantly from those of DF at other locations. This investigation was registered under the clinical trial registration number NCT02867033.

papers.abstract: Hormone receptor-positive, human epidermal growth factor receptor 2-low (HER2-low) metastatic breast cancer (MBC) constitutes the predominant subtype of advanced breast cancer, with most patients eventually developing resistance to endocrine therapy (ET) and cyclin-dependent kinase 4/6 inhibitors (CDK4/6i). This case report describes a 64-year-old woman with hormone receptor (HR)-positive, HER2-low MBC involving lung, pleural, and lymph node metastases who achieved a remarkable and sustained radiographic complete response (rCR) to palbociclib plus fulvestrant, followed by letrozole after fulvestrant injection intolerance. The patient exhibited near-complete regression of metastatic lesions within 18 months and maintained remission for over 6 years, far exceeding the typical median progression-free survival observed in clinical trials. The prolonged remission observed underscores the existence of biologically distinct tumor subsets with exceptional sensitivity to CDK4/6 inhibition, warranting investigation into underlying molecular mechanisms.

papers.abstract: Mixed-grade glioma surgical cohorts exhibit highly variable low-grade glioma (LGG) proportions across studies. This meta-analysis quantifies pooled LGG proportions to provide cohort-level epidemiological benchmarks for researchers, with applications in clinical trial design, health economics, and institutional benchmarking. A single-arm meta-analysis of 191 cohort studies (25,847 patients) with Grade II numerators and denominators from Embase, MEDLINE, PubMed, and Scopus (PRISMA 2020) used Freeman-Tukey random-effects synthesis with Cochrane risk-of-bias assessments; subgroup analyses examined study design, geography, era, molecular specificity, and interventions; sensitivity analyses tested robustness. The pooled LGG proportion was 57% (95% CI: 52%-61%; I²=99%; n=191). Mixed LGG/high-grade gliomas (HGG) cohorts showed 41% (32%-50%; 45 studies, 6,847 patients) versus 82% (77%-88%) in pure WHO Grade II cohorts (25 studies). Surgery-only cohorts demonstrated 46% (33%-59%) versus 86% (74%-98%) with targeted therapies, and 93% (90%-96%) in randomized controlled trials. Sensitivity analyses confirmed stability (50%-62%). In mixed-grade glioma cohorts, an LGG proportion approaching 60% may serve as a cohort-level epidemiological reference for understanding the historical grade composition of mixed surgical series. This meta-analysis primary value lies in applications such as clinical trial design, health economics and epidemiological modeling, and institutional benchmarking. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/, identifier CRD420261323907.

papers.abstract: Prostate cancer remains one of the most frequently diagnosed malignancies and a leading cause of cancer-related mortality among men globally. Its development is driven by a complex interaction of genetic susceptibility, molecular alterations, hormonal signaling, environmental exposures, and lifestyle-related factors. This systematic review synthesizes current evidence on the etiological mechanisms and evolving therapeutic landscape of prostate cancer. A systematic review was conducted according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 guidelines. Literature published between January 2010 and December 2025 was searched in PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science databases. Eligible studies included original research, clinical studies, translational studies, and experimental investigations evaluating prostate cancer etiology, molecular mechanisms, risk factors, biomarkers, or therapeutic interventions. The review included 29 studies encompassing epidemiological cohorts, clinical studies, genomic analyses, tissue-based investigations, and preclinical experimental studies. Evidence demonstrated that prostate cancer etiology involves multiple interconnected pathways, including androgen receptor signaling, DNA repair alterations, genomic instability, chromatin remodeling, metabolic reprogramming, and inflammatory mechanisms. Genetic variants, including single nucleotide polymorphisms and polygenic risk scores, were associated with disease susceptibility, aggressiveness, treatment response, and toxicity outcomes. Therapeutic advances included optimization of androgen deprivation therapy, novel androgen receptor pathway inhibitors, chemotherapy, radiotherapy personalization, bone-targeted therapies, PSMA-directed radioligand therapy, and emerging immunotherapeutic approaches. Biomarker-driven strategies, including genomic classifiers and molecular signatures, showed potential for improving risk stratification and individualized treatment selection. Prostate cancer is a biologically heterogeneous disease requiring integrated approaches that combine molecular understanding with clinical decision-making. Recent advances in precision oncology have expanded therapeutic options beyond conventional treatment paradigms, enabling more personalized management strategies. However, further research is required to improve representation of diverse populations, validate biomarkers across different ethnic groups, and optimize the clinical implementation of emerging targeted and immune-based therapies. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/, identifier CRD420261435105.

papers.abstract: Accurate early diagnosis of Clinically Significant prostate cancer (csPCa) is crucial for improving patient survival rates. This study aimed to develop and validate an interpretable, confidence-based deep learning model for csPCa classification using biparametric MRI (bpMRI). A retrospective analysis was conducted on bpMRI data from 410 patients. A classification model was constructed using the visual geometry group 16-layer (VGG-16) network, incorporating gradient-weighted class activation mapping (Grad-CAM) for visual interpretability, Monte Carlo Dropout (MC-Dropout) for uncertainty estimation, and a rejection mechanism. The model's performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves and area under the ROC curve (AUC). Across all predictions, the confidence-based model achieved an overall accuracy of 79.3% before rejection. At a confidence threshold of 0.8, 80.8% of predictions were retained, among which the selective accuracy was 94.6%, with 99 false-positive and 2 false-negative predictions. Besides, the model's accuracy outperformed that of a senior radiologist (94.6% vs 90.8%). Qualitative Grad-CAM visualization demonstrated that the classifier frequently assigned high activation to MRI regions considered suspicious for csPCa; however, quantitative spatial agreement with lesion annotations was not assessed. This confidence-based model identifies csPCa lesions and provides reliable confidence scores without pixel-level annotations. By rejecting uncertain predictions, it enhances the transparency and safety of clinical decision-making.

papers.abstract: The optimal integration of surgery and definitive chemoradiotherapy (CRT) following modern neoadjuvant immunochemotherapy in stage IIB-IIIA/B non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remains controversial. Although immune checkpoint inhibitors have substantially improved outcomes in both resectable and unresectable disease, prospective randomized data directly comparing surgery and definitive CRT after neoadjuvant immunochemotherapy are lacking. InDuRanS is a prospective, multicenter, randomized, open-label phase II trial conducted in Germany. Patients with (borderline) resectable stage IIB-IIIA/B (N2) NSCLC receive three cycles of neoadjuvant immunochemotherapy with durvalumab plus platinum-paclitaxel. Patients with persistent resectability are randomized 1:1 to surgery or definitive CRT. Both treatment arms receive consolidation durvalumab for up to 12 months. The primary endpoint is 2-year event-free survival in 158 randomized patients. Key secondary endpoints include progression-free survival, overall survival, safety and tolerability, health-related quality of life, and an extensive exploratory translational research program. InDuRanS is the first randomized trial to directly compare surgery versus definitive CRT within a contemporary multimodal treatment sequence incorporating both neoadjuvant and consolidation immunotherapy in stage IIB-IIIA/B NSCLC. Its results are expected to help define optimal local treatment strategies in an evolving therapeutic landscape. InDuRanS is currently active and open to enrollment as of April 2025, with primary completion anticipated in 2028 (NCT06810609).

papers.abstract: Programmable messenger RNA (mRNA) platforms can encode tumor antigens or immunomodulators, enabling coordinated antigen delivery and immune modulation. Yet the literature spans cancer vaccination, delivery engineering, immune biology, and adjacent infectious-disease research, making its structure and evidentiary boundaries difficult to discern. We mapped this cross-domain corpus to clarify its development, organization, and relevance to cancer-associated immune escape. We searched the Web of Science Core Collection (WoSCC) and Scopus on July 29, 2026, for English-language Articles and Reviews published since 2006. The strategy combined programmable or therapeutic mRNA, cancer, and immune-escape-related concepts. R-based analyses summarized the number of publications (NP), total citations (TC), and collaboration patterns; BERTopic modeled titles and abstracts after entity-aware preprocessing. Independent two-author review supported the five topic labels and characterized the outliers, and robustness was assessed across alternative clustering configurations. The dataset comprised 756 publications (NP = 756). Annual output increased more than fourfold in 2021 and reached NP = 182 in 2025. China (NP = 291; 38.49%) and the United States (NP = 146; 19.31%) accounted for nearly 58% of corresponding-author publications. Sichuan University and Frontiers in Immunology ranked first in institutional and journal output, respectively. Nature had the highest retained source-record citation total (TC = 2,326). BERTopic assigned 745 publications to five topics, while 11 of 756 records remained outliers (1.46%). The topics represented mRNA delivery and immunomodulatory cancer-vaccine research (52.1%), SARS-CoV-2 vaccination in oncology and immunotherapy settings (23.6%), therapeutic mRNA cancer-vaccine platforms (13.3%), tumor-antigen discovery and immune-subtype stratification (8.6%), and mRNA-vaccine immunogenicity during autoimmune immunosuppression (2.4%). Publication activity in the retrieved cross-domain corpus expanded rapidly after 2020. The corpus included both direct cancer-mRNA research and adjacent platform or immune-response literature. By distinguishing these components and identifying thematic connections among delivery, antigen selection, immune context, and collaboration, the analysis provides an evidence-navigation framework for prioritizing systematic reviews, mechanistic studies, and clinical evaluation. papers.abstract: Plasma cell-free DNA (cfDNA) is a sensitive, noninvasive tool for monitoring the genomic landscape, heterogeneity, and evolution of cancer, aggregating genetic information from multiple metastatic sites. Here, we study 15,564 cfDNA samples from 12,827 patients with metastatic breast cancer (MBC). We classify samples, deep-sequenced with Guardant360, into MBC subtypes using our trained random forest model. Most patients have variants associated with therapeutic resistance and targetability of approved and experimental therapies, including in PIK3CA, ESR1, PTEN, and AKT1. Frequencies of multiple actionable alterations differed from primary disease, and multiple variants per gene suggest independent resistant clones. The large cohort size enables uncovering clonal co-behaviors, including co-existence and exclusivity of alleles and correlation of allele fractions. cfDNA testing is now recommended in multiple advanced malignancies, including eligibility assessment for clinical trials. We envision this large collection of MBC cfDNA data as an invaluable resource for the design and planning of future clinical trials.

papers.abstract: Herpes simplex virus type 1 (HSV-1) is the leading cause of sporadic viral encephalitis, where uncontrolled viral replication and neuroinflammation drive fatal brain injury. Inherited RIPK3 deficiency predisposes humans to severe disease, but the protective mechanism remains unclear. Using single-cell transcriptomics, genetic knockout models, and analysis of viral replication, interferon production, and cell death across neurons, astrocytes, microglia, and myeloid cells, we show that RIPK3 acts as a cell-type-specific molecular switch. RIPK3 scaffolding promotes interferon response and viral control in multiple central nervous system cell types, while RIPK3-dependent apoptosis limits myeloid accumulation. In contrast, RIPK3 kinase activity in astrocytes triggers necroptosis, leading to neuronal loss and lethal neuroinflammation. Genetic or pharmacological inhibition of RIPK3 kinase suppresses astrocyte necroptosis, enhances IFN responses, preserves brain integrity, and improves survival. These findings suggest that selective modulation of RIPK3 signaling may balance antiviral defense with limitation of neuropathology in HSV-1 encephalitis.

papers.abstract: Apoptosis is triggered by the activation of Caspases leading to irreversible engagement in cell death. However, recent data outline numerous non-apoptotic functions of caspases as well as quite ubiquitous sublethal activation of effector caspases in vivo, opening the question of what drives the bifurcation between cell death and survival. Using quantitative live imaging combined with machine learning and optogenetics in the Drosophila pupal notum (a single-layer epithelium), we reveal the existence of a large heterogeneity of caspase activity thresholds between cells and distinct spatial domains with low or high sensitivity to caspases. We outline the central role of past exposure to sublethal caspase activity, which sensitises cells to apoptosis for several hours and reduces their threshold, and can bias single-cell elimination. Altogether, this work reveals the role of a cell's past history for apoptosis regulation in vivo, which can bias clonal selection and the spatial pattern of cell death.

papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being developed across the Gamma Knife radiosurgery (GKRS) workflow, but its current applications and readiness for clinical integration remain underutilized. This narrative review examines the emerging role of AI in GKRS, with emphasis on treatment planning, outcome prediction, and post-treatment assessment. A structured search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and Scopus was conducted through September 20, 2026 to identify studies applying learning-based AI approaches specifically to GKRS. Eligible studies evaluated AI models using GKRS clinical, imaging, or treatment-planning data, while non-GKRS and non-learning-based studies were excluded. Included studies were synthesized according to major stages of the GKRS workflow. AI applications were identified across tumor segmentation, isocenter selection and treatment planning, prescription and dose-distribution prediction, synthetic computed tomography generation, and plan-quality assessment. Post-treatment applications include longitudinal tumor monitoring and prediction of response, functional outcomes, and toxicity including peritumoral edema and radiation necrosis. Several models demonstrate promising performance, but the evidence remains predominantly retrospective and task-specific, with frequent reliance on single-center or small datasets and limited external or prospective validation. AI has the potential to improve the consistency, efficiency, and personalization of GKRS by supporting specific technical and clinical decisions. Further multicenter validation, prospective evaluation, workflow integration, and demonstration of meaningful clinical benefit are required before routine adoption. AI currently remains a decision-support tool rather than a replacement for radiosurgical expertise.

papers.abstract: To examine the association between neighborhood material deprivation and days at home (DAH) after glioblastoma diagnosis. This population-based retrospective cohort study used linked administrative data from Ontario, Canada, for adults diagnosed with glioblastoma during 2003-2023. Material deprivation was assigned using Ontario Marginalization Index quintiles (Q1, least deprived; Q5, most deprived). The primary outcome was DAH within 365 days, defined as days alive outside acute hospitals, inpatient rehabilitation, and continuing or complex care. The primary analysis included diagnoses through 2022. Median quantile regression adjusted for age, sex, comorbidity, frailty, rurality, and diagnosis year. Secondary outcomes included other DAH horizons and overall survival. Among 9172 adults, 4491 (49.0%) were younger than 65 years and 5435 (59.3%) were male. Median DAH-365 was 249 days (interquartile range, 67-350) in Q1 and 138 (27-332) in Q5. In 8234 complete cases, adjusted median differences versus Q1 were - 8.8 days for Q2 (95% confidence interval [CI], - 19.6 to 2.0), - 14.8 for Q3 (- 27.0 to - 2.6), - 18.3 for Q4 (- 29.4 to - 7.2), and - 36.2 for Q5 (- 51.5 to - 20.9). Median survival was 324 days (95% CI, 306-343) in Q1 and 225 (211-244) in Q5. Greater neighborhood material deprivation was associated with substantially fewer DAH after glioblastoma diagnosis. The adjusted gap exceeding 5 weeks supports investigation of treatment access and supportive care pathways to inform efforts to improve equity.

papers.abstract: Tissue normalisation has emerged as an interesting therapeutic concept in oncology, aiming to correct the structural, metabolic, and immunological tissue abnormalities that enable tumour progression and treatment resistance. Rather than targeting cancer cells directly, this approach aims to re-establish homeostatic tissue architecture, immune surveillance, and metabolic balance. Interventions that target stromal components, such as cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs), immune cells, or stiffness of extracellular matrix (ECM), have been shown to shift tumour cells toward a less aggressive state, underscoring the plasticity of cancer cells and the importance of their interactions with the microenvironment. Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are increasingly recognised as both contributors to tissue dysfunction in tumours and promising tools for restoring tissue homeostasis. EVs circulate across most biofluids and can cross biological barriers to reach distant tissues. They naturally carry nucleic acids, including regulatory miRNAs, along with proteins, lipids, and metabolites that influence cell behaviour, making them attractive tools for tissue normalisation. Moreover, engineered EVs could be designed to deliver targeted "normalisation signals" and hold strong clinical potential as next-generation delivery systems. Here, we explore how EVs, whether native or engineered, can intervene in key tumour-driving processes, including senescence, fibrosis, inflammation, and immune evasion, to shift the microenvironment toward a normalised, less malignant state.

papers.abstract: It remains largely unclear whether oncogenic super-enhancers (SEs) can drive expression of circular RNAs (circRNAs). In this study, we for the first time profiled the comprehensive circRNA landscapes of esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) after suppressing genome-wide SE activities. We identified a novel SE-driven circPRRC2B, as the product of back-splicing of exons 2, 3, 4 and 5 of PRRC2B pre-mRNA, which was controlled by RNA binding protein HuR. Indeed, SE drives high levels of PRRC2B transcription, promotes production of PRRC2B pre-mRNAs, boosts back-splicing of PRRC2B pre-mRNAs, and elevates circPRRC2B expression. ETS1 acts as a key transcriptional factor in SE-driven PRRC2B transcription and circPRRC2B biogenesis. Interestingly, circPRRC2B, but not PRRC2B, could promote proliferation, invasion and metastasis of ESCC in vitro and in vivo. Mechanistically, circPRRC2B binds to TALDO1 and enhances BAP1-mediated TALDO1 de-ubiquitination in ESCC cells. Therefore, circPRRC2B stabilizes and sustains high expression of TALDO1, activates the pentose phosphate pathway (PPP), elevates the glutathione levels via supplying more NADPH via the PPP, inhibits production of reactive oxygen species in mitochondrion, maintains cellular redox equilibrium, and, thus, leads to cancer progression. Importantly, we developed antisense oligonucleotides targeting circPRRC2B which exhibited remarkable inhibition of ESCC growth. Our findings highlighted circPRRC2B as a key target preserving the PPP metabolic flux and redox homeostasis of malignant cells, thereby offering insight into developing novel therapeutics for cancers.

papers.abstract: Circulating tumor DNA-based liquid biopsy is increasingly integrated into cancer care, particularly for detecting minimal residual disease, yet patient perspectives remain poorly understood. This single-center, cross-sectional, mixed-methods study assessed recall, knowledge, and attitudes toward liquid biopsy and circulating tumor DNA among 195 patients (median age 65 years; 63% female) undergoing cancer treatment or follow-up, supplemented by focus groups. Although 65% reported prior liquid biopsy, this was confirmed in only 44%, and only 10% had heard of circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA). Correct recall and knowledge on ctDNA were higher among patients with neuroendocrine neoplasms and those with postgraduate education. In hypothetical scenarios assuming proven clinical validity and utility, 62-80% supported liquid biopsy-guided clinical action, 74% were comfortable with liquid biopsy replacing tissue biopsy, and 79% accepted its use to guide adjuvant treatment. Most patients anticipated reassurance rather than stress, and 85% expected improved quality of life with home- or general practitioner-based blood sampling. Overall, patients showed high acceptance of clinically actionable liquid biopsy use, driven by trust and perceived clinical benefit.

papers.abstract: Tumors are embedded within complex microenvironments composed of malignant, immune and stromal cells, yet how coordinated cellular organization shapes tumor biology across cancers remains incompletely understood. Here we integrate single-cell transcriptomic profiles from over two million cells spanning 19 human epithelial cancers to construct a comprehensive pan-cancer atlas of tumor microenvironment (TME) organization. We identify cell subsets selectively enriched in tumors compared with normal tissues and show that their relative abundance is associated with clinical outcomes. By clustering tumors according to their cellular composition, we define eight recurrent cellular ecosystem subtypes that capture coordinated variation in immune and stromal architectures across cancer types. Comparative analyses reveal that these ecosystem states are associated with distinct tumor-intrinsic molecular programs, including differences in signaling pathway activity, transcriptional regulation and copy number alterations. We further uncover subtype-specific patterns of ligand-receptor interactions linking malignant cells with immune and stromal compartments and provide independent spatial support for these interactions using spatial transcriptomic data. Together, this work provides a unified framework for tumor ecosystem stratification and highlights cellular organization as a key dimension of tumor heterogeneity with potential implications for precision cancer therapy.

papers.abstract: Spinocerebellar ataxia type 3 (SCA3), also called Machado-Joseph disease, the most common form of autosomal dominant cerebellar ataxia, is caused by a CAG repeat expansion in ATXN3. The mutant protein is prone to aggregation and exerts toxic gain-of-function effects, whereas the wild-type protein has important neuroprotective roles as a deubiquitinase. Current treatment strategies for SCA3 lack specificity for the mutant allele. Identifying genetic variants such as single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in linkage with the pathogenic CAG expansion offers a promising avenue to develop allele-specific therapeutic interventions, like antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs). To address this, we conducted allele-specific, targeted, multiplexed nanopore sequencing on 79 patients with SCA3 from Germany, UK, and Portugal. We identified almost 200 polymorphisms and grouped them into three haplotype blocks on the basis of linkage disequilibrium. These SNPs were strongly associated with the CAG expansion. Genotypic modeling of our subcohorts indicated that targeting only two SNPs from different blocks could enable allele-specific treatment of the majority of European patients with SCA3. We evaluated 17 candidate ASOs targeting SNPs from different haplotype blocks. Seven of these ASOs caused allele-preferential reduction of more than 65%. A single ASO application in two SCA3 iPSC-derived cortical neurons (AX1, AX2) achieved up to 90% reduction of mutant ATXN3. Toxicity assessments together with RNA sequencing analyses in AX1 did not indicate evidence of toxicity or widespread transcriptional perturbations. These findings highlight that characterizing heterozygosity rates offers valuable opportunities for selective ASO therapies. Our proof-of-principle targeting with ASOs demonstrates the feasibility of haplotype-informed allele-specific silencing in ATXN3.

papers.abstract: Amphotericin B remains the gold-standard therapy for invasive fungal infections, but its clinical utility is limited by toxicity arising from poor selectivity for fungal ergosterol over mammalian cholesterol, a challenge that decades of medicinal chemistry have failed to fully overcome. Here, we report mandimycin M16, a polyene macrolide engineered from a unique 5 + 1 polyene scaffold that uncouples antifungal potency from host toxicity. Mandimycin M16 exhibited potent, broad-spectrum activity against 11 tested World Health Organization (WHO) priority fungal pathogens. Unlike amphotericin B, which binds cholesterol, M16 exhibited no detectable cholesterol binding and showed no detectable hemolysis, cytotoxicity, or nephrotoxicity at concentrations up to 128 micrograms per milliliter in vitro and after up to seven daily intravenous doses in mice. Mechanistic studies revealed that mandimycin M16 exerted rapid fungicidal activity through selective recognition of the conjugated C5-C8 diene system present in ergosterol but absent in cholesterol, a mode of sterol discrimination fundamentally different from classical polyenes. In multiple disseminated murine infection models, M16 outperformed liposomal amphotericin B at equivalent doses, achieving up to 3.4 log reduction in fungal burden and 100% survival without detectable renal injury by biomarkers or histopathology. These findings establish that the 5 + 1 polyene architecture enables complete sterol selectivity and molecularly uncouples antifungal potency from host toxicity, providing a next-generation antifungal candidate for the treatment of invasive fungal infections.

papers.abstract: ZIP12, a membrane-bound zinc importer, is up-regulated in the remodeled pulmonary arterioles of patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH). Genetic deletion of its encoding gene, Slc39a12, ameliorates the disease in rodent models. Here, we show that ZIP12 overexpression in human pulmonary artery smooth muscle cells (PASMCs) increased intracellular labile Zn2+ and promoted proliferation. ZIP12 siRNA knockdown attenuated pulmonary hypertension in rodent models. We developed a humanized anti-ZIP12 monoclonal antibody, APL-9796, that normalized intracellular Zn2+ concentration, suppressed proliferation in fibroblasts derived from patients with PAH and PDGF-stimulated PASMCs, and reduced PDGF-induced cytoskeletal remodeling in PASMCs and contractility in PASMCs and engineered pulmonary artery tissues. APL-9796 showed dose-dependent efficacy in humanized Slc39a12 rats, improving cardiopulmonary parameters after induction of pulmonary hypertension and was well tolerated in phase 1 clinical studies. Transcriptomic profiling revealed modulation of several molecular pathways, including those involving AMPK, PPAR, and PI3K-Akt. ZIP12-driven labile Zn2+ signaling underpins the pathogenesis of PAH. Targeting ZIP12 with APL-9796 offers a promising therapeutic strategy.

papers.abstract: Cerebral cavernous malformations (CCMs) constitute the second most common type of intracranial vascular malformations. Cavernomas arise because of somatic or autosomal dominant inherited loss-of-function mutations in CCM genes, forming fragile mulberry-like malformed blood vessel structures that are prone to leak and break. Treatment is limited to surgical removal of solitary cavernomas, and because patients often present with multiple lesions, pharmacological alternatives to surgery are needed. We performed a high-throughput screen of 5200 bioactive molecules in programmed cell death 10 (PDCD10 or CCM3)-deficient mouse endothelial cells, coupled to automated image analysis. This screen identified dabrafenib, a clinically approved BRAF inhibitor, as a compound that restored cell-cell junctions and vascular barrier properties of CCM3-deficient endothelial cells. The potential translatability of dabrafenib was tested in acute and chronic CCM mouse models, where it reduced cerebral lesion burden and suppressed lesion permeability. Dabrafenib also rescued abnormal structural defects present in the developing retina vasculature in an acute CCM mouse model. Mechanistically, dabrafenib targeted extracellular regulated kinase (ERK)5-Krüppel-like factor (KLF)2/4 signaling and suppressed F-actin stress fiber formation in human brain endothelial cells, two potentially independent and central molecular processes involved in CCM pathology. Silencing BRAF did not prevent dabrafenib-induced KLF2/4 inhibition or restoration of cell-cell junctions, suggesting that its dual therapeutic outcome is independent of BRAF pathway inhibition. In conclusion, dabrafenib is a low-molecular weight compound that inhibits cavernoma pathogenesis, suggesting that CCMs could be treated with dabrafenib to block cavernoma growth and vascular leakage.

papers.abstract: Acute graft-versus-host disease (aGVHD), following allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation, and organ rejection are serious immune-mediated complications driven by alloreactive T cells. CTPS1, a crucial enzyme for de novo CTP synthesis, is essential for the proliferation of activated T cells, representing an attractive therapeutic target for controlling T cell-mediated pathologies. In this study, using Ctps1-deficient T cells in fully MHC-mismatched and haploidentical hematopoietic stem cell transplantation models, a complete blockage in the induction of aGVHD is observed in association with significantly reduced alloreactive effector T cell expansion. In skin graft rejection models, expansion of alloreactive Ctps1-deficient T cells is reduced, and graft destruction is delayed but not prevented. Notably, the healing process allows T cells to mediate skin graft rejection independently of CTPS1. Finally, treatment with a specific CTPS1 inhibitor rescues mice from lethal aGVHD. Our results underscore the pivotal role of CTPS1 in driving alloreactive T cell responses, highlighting its potential for aGVHD treatment.

papers.abstract: Defective tumor antigen presentation promotes immune evasion and resistance to immune checkpoint blockade. Here, we identified the short-chain fatty acid propionate as a potent enhancer of major histocompatibility complex class I (MHC class I) antigen presentation. Propionate stabilizes MHC class I on tumor cells, promotes CD8+ T cell infiltration and activation, and suppresses tumor growth. Mechanistically, the E3 ubiquitin (Ub) ligase STUB1 directly interacts with human leukocyte antigen (HLA)-A to mediate K168/K170 polyubiquitination and subsequent degradation. Propionate directly binds STUB1 through hydrogen bonds involving K30 and N34, residues that overlap with the MHC class I-binding interface. This interaction blocks STUB1-mediated MHC class I polyubiquitination, thereby stabilizing MHC class I, enhancing T cell receptor (TCR) engagement and T cell activation, and restraining tumor growth. Importantly, propionate or the propionate-producing probiotic Akkermansia muciniphila markedly enhanced anti-PD-1 efficacy. These findings uncover a non-metabolic moonlighting function of short-chain fatty acids in regulating tumor immunity and provide a rationale for leveraging dietary propionate or propionate-producing probiotics to enhance immune checkpoint therapy.

papers.abstract: Traditional genome-wide association studies have primarily focused on detecting main genotype effects, often overlooking genotype-environment interactions (GxE), which are essential for understanding context-specific genetic effects and refining disease etiology. Here we present fast genotype-environment interaction analysis (fastGxE), a scalable and effective genome-wide GxE method designed to identify genetic variants that interact with environmental factors to influence traits of interest. fastGxE controls for polygenic effects, polygenic interaction effects and noise heterogeneity; it remains robust to the number of environmental factors involved in GxE interactions; and it ensures scalability for genome-wide GxE analysis in large biobank studies, achieving speed improvements of 32.98-126.49 times over existing approaches. We illustrate the benefits of fastGxE through extensive simulations and an in-depth analysis of 32 physical traits and 67 blood biomarkers from the UK Biobank. In real-data applications, fastGxE identifies 7 genomic loci associated with physical traits, including 4 novel ones, and 18 genomic loci associated with blood biomarkers, 12 of which are novel. The new discoveries highlight the dynamic interplay between genetics and the environment, uncovering potentially clinically relevant pathways that could inform personalized interventions and treatment strategies.

papers.abstract: Follicular helper T (TFH) cells are well known for their role in supporting B cell responses. Here, we identify a critical B cell-independent function for TFH cells in sustaining regulatory T (Treg) cells within gut-associated lymphoid tissues (GALT). We demonstrate that TFH cells produce interleukin-2 (IL-2) at the T cell-B cell border and within interfollicular regions and that this localized IL-2 is required to maintain GALT Treg cell homeostasis and restrain the expansion of pathogenic effector T cells. Mice selectively lacking IL-2-producing TFH cells develop colitis and fatal multiorgan inflammation, driven by impaired GALT Treg cell responses and uncontrolled effector T cell activation. Broad-spectrum antibiotic treatment alleviates both intestinal and extraintestinal pathology, indicating that loss of tolerance to commensal-derived antigens is a key driver of disease. Together, these findings define a spatially restricted TFH cell-derived IL-2 niche critical for GALT Treg cell stability and uncover an unexpected immunoregulatory role for TFH cells in maintaining gastrointestinal tolerance beyond B cell help.

papers.abstract: Germinal centers (GCs) form as confined clusters of motile cells within individual lymphoid follicles. The role of confinement in GC B cell evolutionary events is unknown. Here, using mice with reduced GC confinement because of deficiency in Gα13-dependent G-protein-coupled receptor signaling, we observed GC-GC trafficking in confinement-defective lymph nodes (LNs). In multicolor clonal lineage tracing mice, de-confined GCs minimally diversified their color palettes with respect to one another. Spatial B cell receptor sequencing revealed greater clonal crossover between neighboring GCs in the setting of dispersal. The total GC B cell repertoire of LNs with inter-GC exchange also decreased in overall diversity because of increased skewing toward top clones. As an outcome, LNs with de-confined GCs more strongly favored clones responding to accessible epitopes while losing clones binding to other portions of antigen. Together, our findings suggest that confinement supports antibody breadth by moderating the spread of dominant clones and preserving unique trajectories in individual GC responses.

papers.abstract: As whole-genome sequencing (WGS) is increasingly used in clinical and public health contexts, clearer expectations regarding the amount of variation present in the "average" human genome are required to contextualise findings. We analysed WGS data from two large population cohorts: 490,541 individuals in UK Biobank (UKB) and 414,830 individuals in All of Us. Following variant and genotype QC, we aimed to assess the range of neutral and disease-associated variation across six genetically-inferred ancestry groups. The "average" genome contains ~4.3-5.3 million variants, of which ~1.5% are rare (within-cohort allele frequency 10,000 basepairs per genome, and rare autosomal copy number variants > 1 Mb present in ~ 1 in 41 (2.5%) individuals. On average, ~32-42% of variants per person are homozygous and individuals have ~4 unique runs of homozygosity > 1.5 Mb, with marked variation observed across ancestry groups. Of the ~21- 26,000 SNVs/indels per person in coding exons of MANE Select transcripts, ~48% are predicted to alter the protein, of which ~0.8% are high-confidence loss-of-function and ~0.1% have REVEL score > 0.7 suggestive of pathogenicity. Depending upon parental age, the average genome contains ~63 de novo variants, of which ~75-80% are paternal in origin. Considering only rare variants in GenCC-curated monogenic disease-associated genes, the average genome contains ~1-3 ClinVar pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants, ~2-5 high-confidence loss-of-function variants, and ~50 ClinVar variants of uncertain significance. Most ClinVar pathogenic variants are heterozygous in recessive disease genes, consistent with carrier status, and have multiple ClinVar submitters. Finally, applying polygenic scores (PGS) for 28 common diseases within UKB, we estimate that the average person is in the top 10% for ~3 conditions, and around 1 in 5 people are in the top 1% for at least one PGS. The ubiquity of genetic variation in individuals has important implications for policy-makers considering genomic screening and clinicians counselling families. The continued underrepresentation of many global populations reflects a broader limitation of contemporary genomic research, underscoring the need for more inclusive datasets worldwide in order to enable equitable precision medicine.

papers.abstract: Recent years have witnessed the surge of human-machine interfaces (HMIs) for various applications. Olfaction is a fundamental chemical sense crucial to perception, memory, and emotion. Current limitations arise from the difficulty of accurately capturing, transmitting, and reproducing odor signals, and the lack of standardized, network-enabled platforms. This work presents an internet of things (IoT)-enabled olfactory interface for remote odor sensing and stimulation. The system integrates an artificial intelligence-assisted odor sensing platform with a wearable piezoelectric olfactory actuation system. We demonstrate the design, characterization, and application of this framework, which integrates devices, circuit architecture, and software algorithms. Applications in medical contexts include psychophysical testing to study olfactory pathways and evaluate sensory loss. We further showcase multisensory stimulation through integrated olfactory and gustatory interfaces for enhanced immersion. This study establishes a scalable framework for IoT-based olfactory interaction, advancing HMIs toward a future that includes the long-overlooked chemical senses.

papers.abstract: Water oceans in large icy moons and exoplanets are isolated from the rocky interior by thick layers of high-pressure ice, which hinder the direct release of nutrients and organics derived from water-rock interaction to the ocean. Possible uptake of these bio-essential compounds into high-pressure ice phases could regulate their availability in the ocean, but this process is poorly constrained. Here, we measured partition coefficients of glycine and alanine into ices VI and VII under elevated temperature-pressure conditions using a diamond-anvil cell. We observed moderate compatibility of glycine and alanine with partition coefficients: Kp,glycine = 0.14 and 0.40 in ices VI and VII, respectively; Kp,alanine = 0.21 and 0.35 in ices VI and VII, respectively. First-principles calculations suggested that amino acids could be incorporated into high-pressure ice's lattice via cogrowth. Compatibility of amino acids into high-pressure ices would favor their transport in large extraterrestrial oceans, opening an avenue to habitability.

papers.abstract: The bite of a female mosquito is the critical point of pathogen transmission, yet the fine-scale biting dynamics on human skin remain unknown. Here, we combine high-speed videography, deep-learning-based tracking, and electrophysiology to analyze biting dynamics of the malaria vector Anopheles coluzzii in real time at the human skin interface. We uncover a previously uncharacterized synchronization of mouthpart and leg movements during probing and identify five distinct below skin sub-behaviors: piercing, vessel searching, blood ingestion, retraction, and withdrawal. We show that disruption of the orco and IR76b chemosensory genes can alter some components of normal biting but these effects are subtle, suggesting possible plasticity in direct-contact chemosensation and mosquito bite execution. Comparative analyses show genus-specific biting strategies between An. coluzzii and Aedes aegypti linked to distinct ways they find blood vessels. Our findings indicate that female mosquitoes exhibit a complex synchronization of body parts at the bite site via motor and chemosensory processes.

papers.abstract: International conservation goals have driven rapid expansion of protected areas. This growth has favored quantity over quality, and often results in residual reserves (i.e., areas where species already experience minimal anthropogenic impact). Spatial prioritization is commonly used to help design protected area networks that represent species while minimizing costs to stakeholders. This approach can result in the siting of protected areas that do not decrease impacts on species of conservation concern. Here, we show how measures of cumulative impacts on species can be used in a spatial prioritization to site protected areas to reduce impacts on species of conservation concern. We use a trait-based vulnerability framework and anthropogenic stressor maps to quantify cumulative impacts from four human activities, and incorporate those impacts into spatial prioritizations. We demonstrate that the inclusion of cumulative impacts on species in spatial prioritization can more efficiently protect biodiversity, balance socioeconomic objectives, and avoid residual reserve outcomes.

papers.abstract: The temporomandibular joint (TMJ) is essential for oral functions such as chewing, speaking, and swallowing. Temporomandibular disorders that impair these functions notably reduce patients' quality of life, and few therapeutic strategies are available to ameliorate these conditions. Here, we identify the neurotrophin receptor (p75NTR) as a central regulator of mandibular condylar cartilage development, mechanoadaptation, and homeostasis. p75NTR loss causes condylar and disc hypoplasia, reduced chondrocyte number, impaired load-induced anabolism, and accelerated degeneration. Conditional deletion experiments demonstrate chondrocyte-autonomous requirements for the brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF)-p75NTR axis, which activates phosphoinositide 3-kinase AKT serine/threonine kinase and p38 mitogen-activated protein kinase signaling to promote proliferation and chondrogenic differentiation while restraining apoptosis. Degenerative human condyles exhibit reduced p75NTR expression levels. Together, these data establish p75NTR as a molecular hub integrating neurotrophic and mechanical cues to preserve postnatal TMJ architecture and highlight the BDNF-p75NTR axis as a potential therapeutic target.

papers.abstract: Crocodylians are iconic thermophiles. Over 250 million years, crocodile-line archosaurs endured hyperthermals, climatic and range shifts, and two mass extinctions. Whether this niche conservatism reflects a deep evolutionary constraint or recent adaptation to novel climates remains unclear. We integrate present-day occurrences with a time-scaled phylogeny of >400 fossil and extant species. Niche models calibrated on living crocodylians were projected across 245 million years and compared with paleophylogeographic reconstructions. Macroevolutionary model fitting shows that temperature and precipitation exhibit strong phylogenetic structure, best described by bounded Ornstein-Uhlenbeck dynamics, indicating long-term niche conservatism. Poleward expansions in warm intervals and contractions in cool phases reflect tracking of conserved optima rather than niche evolution. Unlike non-avian dinosaurs, low-latitude suitability persisted across all but the most extreme end-Cretaceous scenarios, with recovery expanding from tropical refugia. Thermal and precipitation regimes shifted near the Cenomanian/Turonian hyperthermal (∼93.9 Ma) and Eocene/Oligocene aridification transition (∼33.9 Ma), respectively. Climatic niche conservatism is therefore ancient in crocodile-line archosaurs, but not completely static.

papers.abstract: Omnipresent in biology, fibrous networks like collagen possess unique properties: dynamic network via crosslinking and degradation. This intrinsic adaptivity plays a critical role in regulating cell behavior via cell-matrix interactions. Built from biological building blocks, however, these networks are challenging to manipulate or even control. Here, we introduce dynamic network regulation via photochemical control in a synthetic and fibrous highly biomimetic hydrogel. As a proof-of-concept, we demonstrate that the dynamic control over the mechanical properties of this adaptive in vitro model can be used to modulate cell spreading and mechanotransduction in three-dimensional (3D) mesenchymal stromal cell cultures. Our approach not only opens the door to on-demand mechanically adaptive gels with unprecedented control, but simultaneously offers easy processibility and cell extraction of the used synthetic gel.

papers.abstract: A continuous transition between phases hosting distinct excitations-bosonic magnons versus fermionic spinons-is a long-sought phenomenon in quantum magnetism, analogous to the confinement-deconfinement transition in quantum chromodynamics. We report evidence for such a transition in the triangular-lattice antiferromagnet thallium ytterbium disulfide. Antiferromagnetic order develops below TN ≈ 0.53 kelvin. A c-axis field suppresses this order, driving the system into a gapless quantum spin liquid with a spinon Fermi surface above [Formula: see text], evidenced by a finite residual linear term in thermal conductivity, a Pauli-like susceptibility, and a temperature-independent nuclear magnetic resonance Knight shift. Approaching [Formula: see text] from above, the scattering rate of itinerant excitations is strongly enhanced, while their density of states shows no critical enhancement, atypical of conventional magnetic quantum criticality. These results point to a continuous confinement-deconfinement transition governed by fractionalized excitations beyond the Ginzburg-Landau paradigm.
