papers.abstract: Invasive lobular carcinoma (ILC) is known to exhibit distinct metastatic patterns compared with carcinoma of no special type (NST); however, little is known about its specific propensity for central nervous system (CNS) and leptomeningeal (LM) involvement, particularly in estrogen receptor (ER)-positive/human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-negative subtype. We leveraged a multicenter study of 1710 patients with advanced breast cancer (BC). We recorded site of first metastatic recurrence and occurrence/type of the first CNS event. The study endpoints were CNS-free survival, LM-free survival, and post-LM survival. The risk of LM as the first CNS event across histological types was evaluated using a competing-risk framework. Among 1587 patients with known tumor histology, 15.5% had ILC. Within the ER-positive/HER2-negative BC cohort (n = 669), 31.5% of patients developed a CNS event. ILC and NST were associated with similar metastatic CNS-free survival [hazard ratio (HR) 1.30, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.95-1.77, P = 0.095]. In contrast, metastatic LM-free survival was significantly and independently shorter in ILC versus NST (multivariate analysis of LM events without concurrent brain metastases, adjusted HR 4.94, 95% CI 1.57-15.83, P = 0.006). Consistently, Fine-Gray competing-risk analysis confirmed a significantly higher risk of LM involvement as the first CNS event for ILC versus NST (adjusted subdistribution hazard ratio 5.07, 95% CI 1.57-16.41, P = 0.007). Among patients with ER-positive/HER2-negative BC and LM disease, ILC was associated with worse post-LM survival compared with NST (HR 2.79, 95% CI 1.03-4.17, P = 0.040). In patients with ILC presenting with extracranial metastatic disease, we observed similar LM-free survival between those treated with cyclin-dependent kinase 4 and 6 inhibitors and those who were not (P = 0.286). In patients with ER-positive/HER2-negative advanced BC, ILC was independently associated with a higher cumulative incidence of LM as the first CNS event than NST. Patients with ILC who developed LM also experienced poorer post-LM survival. These findings highlight the need for heightened clinical awareness and support prospective studies evaluating earlier LM detection in this population.

papers.abstract: Cabozantinib, a promising tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI), has recently been approved by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) to treat hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). However, the objective response rate (ORR) of cabozantinib as monotherapy is low. Therefore, there is an urgent need to develop cabozantinib-based combination therapy. RNA-sequencing was used to analyse the gene expression alterations in HCC cells after cabozantinib treatment. A luciferase reporter assay was used to measure TFEB transcriptional activity. In vitro and in vivo studies were applied to assess the effect of cabozantinib in combination with autophagy inhibitors on HCC. Our results showed that cabozantinib induces autophagic flux, which protects HCC cells from cabozantinib-induced growth inhibition and apoptosis. Further mechanistic studies showed that cabozantinib upregulates Acetyl-CoA Synthetase 2 (ACSS2) and promotes its nuclear translocation, which subsequently activates transcription factor EB (TFEB). TFEB then binds to lysosomal and autophagy gene promoter regions, thereby promoting lysosomal biogenesis and inducing autophagy. In addition, the combination use of an ACSS2 inhibitor or chloroquine (CQ) enhances the antitumor efficacy of cabozantinib in HCC both in vitro and in vivo. Our study proposes a novel molecular mechanism of cabozantinib and provides insights into cabozantinib-based combination therapy for HCC.

papers.abstract: Despite long-standing immunization programs, pertussis remains a major cause of vaccine-preventable mortality, particularly among infants. Here we present a primary assessment of global pertussis incidence, mortality and disability-adjusted life years across 204 countries and territories from 1990 to 2023. We show that despite short-term pandemic-period fluctuations, the dominant global pattern from 1990 to 2023 was long-term decline: age-standardized mortality decreased by 61.2% and age-standardized incidence by 41.6%. Relative to the anomalously low pandemic-period estimates, incidence and mortality rebounded by 102.6% (95% uncertainty interval, 77.0-128.2%) and 66.1% (95% uncertainty interval, 2.4-174.5%), respectively, between 2020 and 2023. In 2023 alone, we estimated 18.9 million cases and 115,000 deaths attributable to pertussis. This burden remains profoundly inequitable and inversely correlated with the sociodemographic index; sub-Saharan Africa now accounts for roughly 65% of global deaths, with the highest population-adjusted risk concentrated among infants younger than 6 months. Our findings highlight a modeled geographic concentration of pertussis mortality and support strengthening timely infant vaccination, maternal immunization where recommended and feasible and robust surveillance in highly susceptible regions.

papers.abstract: Measles remains a leading cause of vaccine-preventable burden among children, particularly in low-income settings. Despite decades of progress, there are indications of measles resurgence due to stagnation in vaccine coverage. Here, using the Global Burden of Diseases, Injuries and Risk Factors Study (GBD) 2023, we systematically assessed measles incidence, mortality, disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) and vaccine coverage (measles-containing vaccine 1 (MCV1) and measles-containing vaccine 2 (MCV2)) among children under 5 years of age across 204 countries and territories from 1990 to 2023. Between 1990 and 2019, global measles incidence and mortality declined by approximately 80% and 90%, respectively, but rebounded sharply after 2020, with 15.6 million cases and 118,000 deaths estimated in 2023 (+40% and +12% increases, respectively, between 2019 and 2023). Sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia continue to bear the highest burden. Global MCV1 coverage rose from 67.2% in 1990 to 83.6% in 2019 but stalled and declined slightly to 81.0% by 2023; MCV2 coverage increased from 14.4% in 1990 to 68.4% in 2019 and reached 71.4% by 2023. Several regions remain well below the Immunization Agenda 2030 (IA2030) target of 90% coverage. The recent measles resurgence underscores the fragility of global immunization progress and the urgent need to restore routine vaccination, close immunity gaps and strengthen outbreak preparedness.

papers.abstract: Adenomyosis has been shown to reduce live birth rates and increase the risk of pregnancy loss. The diagnosis is often established by ultrasonographic assessment using the revised Morphological Uterus Sonographic Assessment (MUSA) criteria. However, the reproductive impact of specific sonographic features remains unclear. A systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted to investigate whether individual ultrasonographic adenomyosis features influence pregnancy outcomes in women with infertility or pregnancy loss. We searched MEDLINE (PubMed), Embase, Cochrane Library (CENTRAL), Web of Science, Scopus, and Google Scholar (most recent 200 records) from inception to May 11th, 2026. Observational and interventional studies reporting specific ultrasonographic features of adenomyosis in women with infertility and/or pregnancy loss were included. Primary outcomes were clinical pregnancy, live birth, and pregnancy loss. Two reviewers independently extracted data and assessed risk of bias using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale and Joanna Briggs Institute critical appraisal tools, as appropriate by study design. Meta-analyses were performed using random-effects models, with common-effects models applied where appropriate; remaining evidence was synthesised narratively. Certainty of evidence was assessed by GRADE. The protocol was registered on PROSPERO (CRD420251077005). Of 2322 records screened, 29 studies comprising 19,510 patients (7569 with adenomyosis) were included. Diffuse adenomyosis was associated with lower odds of live birth compared with no adenomyosis (OR 0.52, 95% CI 0.34-0.79; I2 = 63%), as well as internal adenomyosis compared with no adenomyosis (OR 0.49 95% CI 0.42-0.57 I2 = 0%). Narrative synthesis suggested poorer reproductive outcomes with adenomyosis features located near the endometrium and with larger uterine volume. The overall certainty was low or very low for 20 out of 21 outcomes, and moderate for one, primarily driven by imprecision and indirectness related to variation in diagnostic criteria across studies. Reproductive outcomes in adenomyosis vary according to specific ultrasonographic features, supporting feature-based reporting beyond a binary diagnosis. Substantial clinical and methodological heterogeneity, including inconsistent ultrasonographic diagnostic criteria, variable application of MUSA definitions, and differences in fertility treatment protocols, warrants cautious interpretation of pooled estimates. Standardised definitions and reporting of adenomyosis features are needed to improve evidence synthesis and clinical translation. The Novo Nordisk Foundation and the Danish Research Council.

papers.abstract: Tecovirimat was developed as an antiviral countermeasure against orthopoxviruses and approved by the US Food and Drug Administration Animal Rule based on efficacy in preclinical studies and clinical pharmacokinetic and safety trials. However, recent randomised clinical trials in patients with mpox who initiated tecovirimat an average of 6-9 days after onset of symptoms did not show improvement in time to resolution of skin lesions. Here, we evaluated whether timing of tecovirimat initiation influenced antiviral efficacy following mpox infection in nonhuman primates and defined the therapeutic window for treatment initiation. In this randomised preclinical study, 32 cynomolgus macaques were challenged intravenously with 1 × 106 TCID50 mpox clade IIb virus. Oral tecovirimat (10 mg/kg, once daily for 14 days) treatment was initiated on Day 2 (post-exposure and pre-symptomatic), Day 5 (early symptomatic), or Day 9 (peak symptomatic) after mpox challenge, or no treatment was given as a control group. The primary study endpoint was area under the curve (AUC) and peak numbers of progressive skin lesions. The secondary endpoint was AUC and peak levels of plasma viral loads. Additional analyses included total skin lesions, adaptive immune responses, and transcriptomic signatures. Treatment adherence was 100%. All tecovirimat-treated animals survived to study completion on Day 28, whereas two untreated control animals required early euthanisation on Days 16 and 17. Tecovirimat efficacy was time-dependent. Progressive skin lesion AUC was significantly lower when treatment was initiated on Day 2 (P 0.99). In this randomised preclinical study, tecovirimat demonstrated antiviral therapeutic efficacy but only when initiated early prior to peak viraemia. These findings emphasise the importance of early initiation of treatment and define the therapeutic window for optimal tecovirimat treatment in nonhuman primates. This study was supported by SIGA Technologies.

papers.abstract: Crimean-Congo haemorrhagic fever virus (CCHFV) is a highly pathogenic, tick-borne orthonairovirus responsible for severe human disease, yet no approved vaccines or therapeutics exist. The glycoprotein precursor (GPC), including its GP38, Gn, and Gc components, and the nucleoprotein (NP) have been explored as vaccine targets with varying success. A chimpanzee adenoviral vector (ChAdOx) vaccine encoding full-length GPC previously conferred complete protection in mice, supporting Phase I evaluation. However, the essential protective components and mechanisms of vaccine-induced immunity remain unclear. We evaluated ChAdOx2 vaccines encoding individual GPC subunits (GP38, Gn, or Gc), full-length GPC, or NP in a lethal interferon receptor-deficient mouse model. Protective efficacy and immune responses were assessed to define protective immunogens and mechanisms. Single-dose vaccination with ChAdOx2-GP38 or ChAdOx2-Gc conferred complete survival (6/6 per group; both p = 0.0005 vs PBS), with minimal histopathology and viral RNA burden at the 21-day study endpoint, comparable to full-length GPC (6/6; p = 0.0005 vs PBS). ChAdOx2-NP likewise conferred complete survival (6/6; p = 0.0008 vs PBS) and elicited robust NP-specific immune responses. In contrast, ChAdOx2-Gn conferred partial survival (2/6; p = 0.0101 vs PBS), while low-dose GPC vaccination provided limited protection (1/6; p = 0.0617 vs PBS) with impaired IgG responses while preserving T-cell responses. Immunological analyses showed that GP38, Gc, and full-length GPC constructs induced robust antibody responses with similar Fcγ receptor engagement and limited neutralising activity. These findings identify GP38 and Gc as individually protective immunogens while reinforcing GPC and NP as effective vaccine targets. Together, these data support roles for non-neutralising antibodies and T-cell responses in protection against CCHFV and continued development of ChAdOx-vectored vaccines for clinical use. papers.abstract: Expanded CAG/CTG repeats cause more than 15 different diseases that all remain without a disease-modifying treatment. Because repeat length accounts for most of the variation in disease severity, contracting CAG/CTG repeats presents an attractive therapeutic avenue. Here, we show that the CRISPR-Cas9 nickase targeted to CAG/CTG repeats leads to efficient repeat contractions in Huntington's disease (HD) patient-derived neurons and astrocytes and in myotonic dystrophy type 1 patient-derived neurons. The approach was allele selective and free of detectable off-target mutations. Injection of the Cas9 nickase into the striatum of the R6/1 mouse model of HD using adeno-associated viral vectors led to repeat contractions in more than half of striatal neurons. Upon injection, we observed a reduction in the number of inclusion bodies, an improved gene expression profile, and amelioration of locomotion deficits in the open field test. The effects were greater than expected from the contractions induced, suggesting that non-cell autonomous mechanisms may be involved. Our results provide the proof of concept that correction of CAG/CTG repeats can improve HD phenotypes in a mouse disease model.

papers.abstract: Choline kinase α (ChoKα) is a biomarker of lung cancer, is overexpressed in 60% of human pulmonary malignancies, and is associated with an aggressive phenotype and poor clinical outcome. Patients with lung cancer who undergo surgery have a recurrence rate of 30 to 50%, indicating a potential need for better tumor detection modalities. A near-infrared fluorescent ChoKα-targeting imaging agent, JAS239 (λex, λem: 745, 775 nanometers), was developed for intraoperative identification of tumors, their margins, and local metastases. In lung cancer cells, JAS239 inhibited phosphocholine production, reduced viability in a dose-dependent manner, and accumulated in the cytoplasm where ChoKα is active. JAS239 had favorable pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics for imaging metastatic lung lesions in mice. In situ and ex vivo fluorescence imaging of primary lung tumors in a canine clinical trial showed distinct tumor identification and margin delineation with a tumor-to-background ratio of 5.0 ± 0.6 and a contrast-to-variance ratio of 2.0 ± 0.2 at 0.5 milligram/kilogram. Fluorescence imaging identified a clinically significant event where an occult lesion was found after primary tumor resection. Fluorescence imaging also identified a close surgical margin, which prompted further investigation. Immunohistochemistry for ChoKα showed overexpression in canine lung tumors proportional to tumor fluorescence. Ex vivo human tumor painting demonstrated preferential JAS239 localization with a tumor-to-background ratio of 1.5 ± 0.1 and a contrast-to-variance ratio of 0.9 ± 0.1. These studies establish JAS239 as a safe and effective imaging agent for intraoperative lung tumor detection, warranting further evaluation for human patients with lung cancer.

papers.abstract: Successful hematopoietic cell transplant requires immunosuppression to prevent graft-versus-host disease (GVHD), a lethal, T cell-mediated complication. The phase 3 BMT CTN 1703 trial demonstrated superior GVHD-free/relapse-free survival for posttransplant cyclophosphamide (PT-Cy)-based GVHD prophylaxis versus tacrolimus/methotrexate (Tac/MTX), but the T cell biology underpinning these outcomes remains unknown. To determine this, 324 patients were coenrolled onto BMT CTN 1801 to investigate the distinct T cell immune reconstitution pathways of these regimens, including extensive evaluation of T cell receptor (TCR) repertoire, via sequencing of 2359 longitudinal samples and 180,432,350 T cells. Multimodal T cell analysis revealed that PT-Cy was associated with pan-T cell deletion followed by delayed T cell expansion from a smaller founder population compared with Tac/MTX. This created a T cell diversity bottleneck, leading to reduced TCR repertoire diversity for 2 years posttransplant. Reduced TCR diversity, more common in patients receiving PT-Cy, was linked to protection against chronic GVHD when patients were analyzed without regard to study arm. Leveraging donor- and host-specific TCR clonal analysis, we determined that PT-Cy-mediated T cell depletion also depleted pathogen-specific TCRs, rendering PT-Cy patients more likely to lack detectable graft-derived pathogen-specific TCRs early after transplant, which was associated with an increased risk of severe infection. This study reveals how distinct immunosuppression strategies uniquely remodel T cell immunity and shape divergent transplant outcomes.

papers.abstract: Whether the anti-inflammatory effects of a Mediterranean diet reflect diet quality itself or accompanying weight loss is unclear. In a 16-week randomized controlled-feeding trial, 53 adults (77% female; mean age 54.7 years) with metabolic risk factors received a fully provided Mediterranean diet or their habitual western diet for 8 weeks, then added twice-weekly fasting days for a further 8 weeks. The primary outcome, high-sensitivity C-reactive protein, did not change during the diet-only phase despite clear dietary separation. After fasting began, C-reactive protein fell in the Mediterranean-diet group relative to controls, alongside greater weight loss, improved insulin sensitivity, and lower blood pressure; lipid improvements had already emerged during the diet-only phase. Multi-omic analyses showed parallel reductions in inflammatory signaling, with gut microbiome composition largely stable. Thus, diet quality alone does not lower inflammation over 8 weeks; negative energy balance and weight loss during fasting appear to be the stronger drivers. This study was registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT02148458).

papers.abstract: Abstract We performed a large-scale genome-wide association study meta-analysis of magnetic resonance imaging-derived liver triglyceride content across 71,488 European-ancestry participants from the UK Biobank, approximately doubling the sample size of previous genome-wide association studies 1 . We identified 60 independent loci, including 31 not previously reported, and estimated the single nucleotide polymorphism-based heritability of liver triglyceride content at 25%. Integrative fine-mapping and gene-prioritization analyses nominated candidate effector genes for 48 loci. Of the 31 newly identified variants, 14 were validated in meta-analyses of clinically diagnosed metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (42,163 cases and 1,646,254 controls). People in the highest versus lowest decile of a polygenic risk score for liver triglyceride content had 2.71-fold higher odds of cirrhosis and 7.47-fold higher odds of hepatocellular carcinoma. Plasma proteins associated with the liver triglyceride polygenic risk score were enriched for metabolic remodeling and inflammatory pathways, with liver-enriched protein signatures increasing and visceral adipose signatures decreasing with higher genetic risk. Together, these findings refine the genetic architecture of liver triglyceride content, linking polygenic susceptibility to downstream metabolic and inflammatory pathways and providing insights into the genetic basis of steatotic liver disease.

papers.abstract: Characterizing noncoding variant function remains an important challenge in human genetics. Genomic deep learning models have emerged as a promising approach to enable in silico prediction of variant effects. These models include supervised sequence-to-activity models, which predict molecular phenotypes such as genome-wide chromatin states or gene expression levels directly from DNA sequence, and self-supervised genomic language models. Here we review progress in leveraging these models for noncoding variant effect prediction. We describe practical considerations for making such predictions and categorize the types of ground-truth data used to evaluate variant effect predictions, providing insight into the settings in which current models are most useful. Our Review highlights key considerations for practitioners and opportunities for improvement in model development and evaluation.

papers.abstract: Here we present DynaVelo, a generative neural ordinary differential equation model that learns the joint dynamics of gene expression and transcription factor (TF) motif activity from single-cell multiome data. DynaVelo learns a functional form of the vector field, such that the model can be perturbed in silico and not only used to draw trajectories. We show that DynaVelo recovers the bifurcating in vivo dynamics of wild-type murine germinal center (GC) B cells and reveals how these dynamics change under heterozygous loss of epigenetic regulators Arid1a and Ctcf. In silico perturbation yields dynamic and cell-state-specific gene regulatory networks (GRNs) that recover known TF-to-gene edges in the wild-type GC GRN and predicts those that are disrupted in mutants. Perturbing Arid1aHet GCs in silico identified Ctcf, Stat3 and Bcl6 as rescue targets for Arid1a loss. In vivo experiments in double-heterozygous mice confirmed rescue of the Arid1aHet dark-zone phenotype in all three cases, and multiome profiling of Arid1aHet;CtcfHet GCs validated the predicted shift toward wild-type dynamics.

papers.abstract: Transcriptomic measurement technologies provide powerful approaches to understand biology but are limited to providing either a high-resolution snapshot at a moment in time or a low-resolution history of transcription constrained to a few genes over a narrow time range. Here, we introduce the 'recordanelle', a single-component synthetic organelle capable of recording the transcriptome in human cells. Recordanelles are composed of a mitochondrial membrane anchor, a condensate assembler and a poly(A)-binding protein. We demonstrate that the recordanelle can be engineered to recruit engineered RNAs or a sampling of up to 90% of all endogenous mRNAs and protect them over several days. We further show that transient and dynamic transcriptional responses resulting from inducible promoters or interferon signaling are preserved throughout time within the recordanelle at the single-cell level. This work provides a nondisruptive and unbiased transcriptome-wide single-cell RNA recording technology to enable a deeper understanding of biology.

papers.abstract: Neutrophils, the most abundant leukocytes in human blood, have multifaceted roles in health and disease. Here we assembled a single-cell atlas of human neutrophils (SCAHN) by integrating transcriptome data from 1 million human neutrophils from 781 samples and 43 independent datasets. Using SCAHN, we identified multiple neutrophil subsets with distinct functions across tissues and robust changes in gene expression and subset proportions in infection, cancer, immune suppression and sex differences at single-cell resolution. Cross-species reference mapping of mouse and nonhuman primate neutrophils onto SCAHN revealed both conserved and species-specific features. Using 17,023 bulk blood transcriptome profiles from 40 datasets, we found that neutrophil-specific signatures predicted mortality in acutely ill patients at presentation, were associated with cancer diagnosis and survival, and correlated with metabolic dysfunction and long-term all-cause mortality. Our study highlights how neutrophil biology can improve immune risk stratification and develop effective diagnostic and therapeutic strategies.

papers.abstract: Obesity affects 15% of children aged 2 to 5 years and 22% of children aged 6 to 11 years in the US. Obesity in children is associated with dyslipidemia, hypertension, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, and obstructive sleep apnea. Compared with normal-weight peers, children with obesity have lower quality of life and are 5 times more likely to have obesity in adulthood. Body mass index (BMI; calculated as weight in kilograms divided by height in meters squared) is used to identify children at risk for excess adiposity, and guidelines recommend that clinicians screen for obesity using BMI starting at age 2 years. Among children, obesity is defined using standardized age- and sex-specific growth charts, with obesity defined as BMI in the 95th or higher percentile and severe obesity as BMI of 120% or greater of the 95th percentile. Obesity treatment in children includes intensive health behavior and lifestyle treatment, consisting of at least 26 contact hours of face-to-face group or family-based activities that incorporate nutrition, physical activity, and behavior change education delivered to the child and caregivers over a 3- to 12-month period. Intensive health behavior and lifestyle treatment reduces BMI by 0.7 compared with children who do not participate in intensive health behavior and lifestyle treatment. The only obesity pharmacotherapy currently approved by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for children younger than 12 years is setmelanotide, a melanocortin-4 receptor agonist, which is indicated for 3 forms of rare monogenic obesity (LEPR, POMC, and PCSK1 genetic variants), Bardet-Biedl syndrome, and acquired hypothalamic obesity. Liraglutide is currently only FDA approved for youth aged 12 years or older; however, a randomized clinical trial among children aged 6 to younger than 12 years demonstrated that, compared with placebo, liraglutide reduced BMI by 7.4%. Metabolic and bariatric surgery is rarely used in children younger than age 12 years and evidence supporting its use in children is limited. Early identification and treatment of obesity during childhood may reduce risk of type 2 diabetes, dyslipidemia, hypertension, and mortality in adulthood. Obesity in children is associated with chronic disease, such as hypertension, and with poor quality of life. Evidence-based treatment for obesity in children includes intensive health behavior and lifestyle treatment, and pharmacotherapy may provide additional benefit, although short- and long-term safety and efficacy data are limited. Early identification and treatment of obesity during childhood may reduce risk of type 2 diabetes, dyslipidemia, hypertension, and mortality in adulthood.

papers.abstract: Marine heatwaves (MHWs) are devastating extreme ocean temperature events whose frequency and severity have surged under global warming, threatening marine ecosystems and fisheries. Yet, the fundamental mechanisms that control their intensity and persistence remain incompletely understood. Here, using a submesoscale-permitting global model simulation validated by long-term observational and reanalysis data, this study reveals a previously overlooked submesoscale feedback that exerts a critical control on MHW severity. It is demonstrated that the submesoscale-induced vertical heat flux suppresses the intensity and persistence of atmosphere-driven MHWs in winter via a negative feedback mechanism. Enhanced air-sea net heat flux strengthens stratification and shoals the mixed layer, weakening submesoscale vertical heat transport by 19.4%, reducing MHW intensification by 18.1%, and accelerating decay by 21.7%. This missing regulatory mechanism indicates that models ignoring the submesoscale feedback likely overestimate MHW severity, with critical implications for future climate projections.

papers.abstract: Bacteriophages (phages), viruses that exclusively infect bacteria, coexist with their bacterial hosts across diverse environments at densities exceeding 10 7 per milliliter in marine surface waters, 10 8 per milliliter in soils, and 10 9 per milliliter in the human gut. In contrast, phage lysis of bacterial populations within well-mixed in vitro environments select for the emergence of phage-resistant bacterial mutants, which, in turn, select for host-range expansion phage mutants and, typically, the collapse of phage populations altogether. This gap in outcome raises a question: What enables long-term phage-bacteria coexistence? Here, we show how interactions in space can facilitate stable coexistence and long-range transport of virulent phage along with migrating bacteria. Combining theory, simulation, and experiments across multiple phage-bacteria systems, we reveal a chemotaxis-driven mechanism that robustly stabilizes coexistence and dispersal of virulent phages with migrating hosts. These findings suggest the ecological relevance of spatial interaction mechanisms that reinforce stability between antagonistic partners in the absence of perpetual cycles of defense and counterdefense, which may be broadly applicable across phage-bacteria systems.

papers.abstract: Enterococcus faecalis is an opportunistic pathogen that persists in biofilm-associated infections despite robust neutrophil recruitment. How E. faecalis evades neutrophils remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated how E. faecalis biofilms alter effector functions in human neutrophils and a murine wound infection model. We found that E. faecalis biofilm suppresses neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) formation, bacterial engulfment, and neutrophil-mediated control of biofilm growth. This suppression is partly driven by production of lactic acid through the lactate dehydrogenases (LDHs) of E. faecalis, which acidifies the extracellular environment, lowers neutrophil intracellular pH, and disrupts glycolysis, the tricarboxylic acid cycle, and the oxidative pentose phosphate pathway. In a murine wound infection model, loss of LDH increased neutrophil recruitment and NETosis. We also found that high bacterial density, a defining feature of biofilms, suppresses NETosis through a lactic acid-independent mechanism. Collectively, these findings identify biofilm immune evasion strategies mediated by bacterial metabolism and the high-density structural organization of biofilm-associated bacteria.

papers.abstract: Thioester domains (TEDs) represent a family of bacterial adhesin domains that mediate covalent anchoring to target ligands via an intramolecular thioester bond. Although the broad distribution of TEDs among Gram-positive bacteria suggests a critical functional role, the biological significance of this covalent mechanism remains unclear. In this study, we demonstrated that TED-mediated covalent anchoring is reversible and that its equilibrium is regulated by pH. Specifically, SfbI-TED from group A Streptococcus binds tightly to fibrinogen at physiological pH, whereas mild acidification to pH 6.0 induces rapid dissociation of the complex. Thermodynamic analyses indicated that this pH responsiveness is largely dictated by the intrinsic pH sensitivity of the thioester-mediated acyl transfer reaction conserved within TEDs, rather than by surface residues specific to individual TEDs. Similar pH-dependent behavior was observed in phylogenetically distinct TEDs, suggesting that pH-responsive adhesion is likely to be a broadly shared feature of TED-containing adhesins across Gram-positive bacteria.

papers.abstract: Glacial-interglacial transitions punctuate Earth's Quaternary climate, accompanied by substantial atmospheric carbon dioxide and ocean carbon storage changes. The cause of atmospheric carbon drawdown during glaciations is uncertain, involving many mechanisms whose interactions are poorly understood. Here, we show that the combined expansion of Antarctic sea ice and associated changes in the meridional overturning efficiently sequester carbon in the ocean abyss, leading to a decline in atmospheric carbon dioxide. In contrast, changes in sea ice and circulation individually result in ocean carbon dioxide outgassing. When sea ice expansion and circulation changes act together, they enhance biological carbon storage by reducing ocean-atmosphere fluxes in the Southern Ocean, without invoking external drivers of the biological pump. This reduction inhibits the outgassing of upwelled remineralized carbon and promotes its resubduction into the abyss. Together, these results reveal a reinforcing feedback linking atmospheric cooling, Antarctic sea ice expansion, and ocean circulation changes to enhanced biological carbon storage and atmospheric carbon dioxide drawdown.

papers.abstract: Breakdown of selection rules and emergence of optical activity in Raman spectroscopy typically signal symmetry-breaking events essential for understanding novel phases of solids. Here, we apply our recently developed rotational anisotropy Raman spectroscopy technique to single-crystal ruthenium dioxide-a compound of recent interest as a candidate workhorse material for altermagnetism yet whose magnetic ground state remains under intense debate. Our data reveal a salient breakdown of selection rules for zone-center phonons, accompanied by clear splitting in the angle-dependent polarimetry plots for the two opposite helicity-nonconserving circularly polarized scattering channels. These observations provide definitive evidence of a previously overlooked symmetry-breaking event, involving either spatial or time-reversal symmetry. In either scenario, the underlying mechanism is likely a bulk hidden order parameter, potentially involving multipole moments of Ruthenium(IV) set by the local crystal field environment. Our work demonstrates how subtle symmetry-breaking events can manifest through lattice dynamics and calls for renewed experimental and theoretical efforts to map the phase diagram of ruthenium dioxide as a system poised near quantum phase transition boundaries.

papers.abstract: Schizophrenia disrupts both how people perceive the world and how they express and act on their thoughts, yet these symptoms are usually studied separately. Using magnetoencephalography during multisensory and motor tasks, we tested whether reduced event-related beta-band (15 to 30 hertz) modulation, a signal implicated in predictive control, provides a candidate neural marker across these domains. Compared to healthy individuals, patients showed diminished beta changes during sensory processing and movement completion, suggesting reduced flexibility in updating internal models. This neural pattern covaried with audiovisual simultaneity-judgment behavior, disorganized natural speech, and greater clinical severity. These findings suggest that distributed beta modulation may serve as a candidate cross-domain marker associated with perceptual, motor, and language disturbances in schizophrenia, motivating future studies that directly test predictive updating mechanisms.

papers.abstract: Injection of pure spin current into superconductors remains a major challenge in superconducting spintronics. Previous studies have primarily focused on spin-polarized quasiparticles and spin-triplet supercurrents, while vortices-ubiquitous topological defects in type-II superconductors-have been theoretically proposed as alternative carriers of spin angular momentum, yet direct experimental evidence is still lacking. Here, we report the vortex-mediated spin current injection in NbSe2/LiAl2Fe3O8(LAFO) bilayer, an Ising superconductor/ferrimagnetic insulator heterostructure. Under an out-of-plane temperature gradient and an in-plane magnetic field, the NbSe2/LAFO bilayer shows a pronounced thermoelectric peak near the upper critical magnetic field, which has the opposite sign to the conventional vortex Nernst signal observed in a single-layer NbSe2. The sign reversal suggests that the vortex flow induced by spin current injection is opposite to the flow driven by the temperature gradient, which is consistent with theoretical mechanisms including spin-vorticity transmutation and the inverse vortex spin Hall effect. By mapping the field-temperature phase diagram, we reveal that the spin current injection occurs exclusively in the vortex liquid phase of NbSe2. Absence of the thermoelectric signal above the superconducting transition temperature further rules out the quasiparticle contribution. Our results establish vortices as efficient carriers of spin information in superconductors, opening a new route towards vortex-mediated superconducting spintronic devices.

papers.abstract: Most small cell lung cancers (SCLCs) exhibit low immunogenicity and intrinsic resistance to immunotherapy, yet the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we identify CREBBP loss, a frequent genetic alteration in SCLC, as a key suppressor of tumor cell-intrinsic immune responses that drives an immune-cold tumor microenvironment in Rb1/Trp53-driven autochthonous mouse models. Consistently, Crebbp deletion promotes immune escape in syngeneic SCLC models. Mechanistically, Crebbp loss suppresses Sting and major histocompatibility complex class-I expression by reducing histone H3 acetylation. Notably, HDAC inhibition restores histone acetylation, reactivates these silenced genes, and induces tumor cell-intrinsic immune responses. Moreover, pharmacological HDAC inhibition synergizes with immune checkpoint blockade to suppress tumor growth in both Crebbp-mutant and Crebbp-wild-type SCLCs, with a more prominent effect in Crebbp-mutant tumors. Collectively, these findings establish CREBBP loss as a key mechanism of immune evasion and immunotherapy resistance in SCLC, highlighting HDAC inhibition as a promising strategy to enhance immunotherapy efficacy.

papers.abstract: Nuclear envelope (NE) reassembly is essential for the zygote-to-totipotency transition in mammalian embryos. Beyond its classical roles in nuclear transport and maintenance of the RanGTP gradient, the function of RanGAP1 in embryonic NE reassembly has remained elusive. Here, we show that RanGAP1 localizes to the early embryonic NE, driving reassembly via a distinct structural mechanism. Trim-Away-mediated RanGAP1 depletion causes two-cell stage arrest and severe NE defects, including nuclear pore complex (NPC) loss, failed reassembly, and aberrant "fishnet" membrane structures. Mechanistically, RanGAP1 establishes a structural paradigm for endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-lamina coupling by recruiting Lamin A/C, B1, and B2 to the ER for coassembly. The acidic domain and SUMO-1 modification at Lys526 (K526) are essential for the NPC localization of RanGAP1. Thus, RanGAP1 orchestrates nuclear lamina (NL) assembly by targeting lamins to the ER. These findings uncover mechanisms of NE reassembly that are critical for early embryogenesis and provide insights into NE-related developmental disorders.

papers.abstract: The kinetochore is an essential structure for the faithful chromosome segregation during mitosis. The 16-protein complex known as the constitutive centromere-associated network (CCAN) localizes the centromere throughout the cell cycle and forms the basis of the kinetochore. Although cryo-electron microscopy has provided a structural model of an individual CCAN unit, how multiple CCAN units are organized within cells remains unclear. Here, using in silico and in vivo analyses, we demonstrate that multiple CCAN units form a spherical shell-like structure in interphase DT40 kinetochores. CENP-T and CENP-N localize to the CCAN shell, whereas the CENP-C cupin domain clusters at the center. Molecular dynamics simulations of CCAN assembly suggest that CENP-C-DNA interactions constrain the orientation of CCAN units, supporting a spherical shell-like organization via CENP-C oligomerization. Super-resolution imaging reveals the spherical shell-like structure at DT40 kinetochores, and CENP-C knockout or expression of a CENP-C DNA binding deficient mutant abolishes the structure, consistent with the simulation-derived model. These findings provide important insights into the spatial organization of functional kinetochores within cells.

papers.abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) remains a health threat, particularly for infants, older adults, and immunocompromised individuals. Although neutralizing antibodies can help limit infection and viral replication, T cells are essential for reducing disease severity. Assessment of age-related declines in T cell function are important for vaccine evaluation. We used intracellular cytokine staining, activation-induced marker, and Meso Scale Discovery assays and single-cell multiomic profiling to evaluate RSV vaccine mRNA-1345 responses in younger and older adults. mRNA-1345 induced comparable CD4+ and CD8+ T cell responses in both cohorts, with CD4+ responses persisting for 24 months. The CD4+ response was strongly T helper 1 (TH1)-polarized, with increased interferon-γ, interleukin-2, and tumor necrosis factor-α and minimal TH2 cytokines. Both CD4+ and CD8+ T cells showed increased polyfunctionality that remained elevated at 2 years. Single-cell and T cell receptor repertoire analyses showed similar Pre-F-specific phenotypes, transcriptional profiles, and clonal overlap across age groups, supporting robust, durable cellular immunity after mRNA-1345 vaccination. These findings indicate shared vaccine-elicited T cell immunity in adults.

papers.abstract: Allosteric modulation of G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) offers promising therapeutic opportunities. Although multiple allosteric binding sites have been identified in GPCRs, whether and how these spatially distinct sites cooperate to regulate receptor activation remain poorly understood. Here, we elucidate the molecular mechanism of cooperative multisite allostery in the dopamine D1 receptor (D1R). We developed two novel D1R positive allosteric modulators (PAMs), UNC9815 and UNC10062, and used cryo-electron microscopy to structurally identify two previously uncharacterized D1R allosteric sites occupied by UNC9815/UNC10062 and another D1R PAM, BMS-A1. Both sites localize to the transmembrane helix (TM) 1 to 7 interface as vertically adjacent allosteric pockets organized in a spatially complementary manner. Our structures demonstrate the simultaneous binding of the chemically distinct PAMs (LY3154207, BMS-A1, and UNC9815/UNC10062) in three nonoverlapping pockets. Concurrent engagement of all three allosteric sites produces pronounced functional cooperativity, increasing dopamine potency by >1000-fold, thereby demonstrating that coordinated multisite modulation can achieve substantial pharmacological amplification beyond the limits imposed by single PAM administration. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations revealed that multisite PAM engagement restricts intracellular loop 3 dynamics and stabilizes the TM7-NPxxY activation motif, effects not achieved by binding of LY3154207 alone, thereby biasing the receptor toward a more stabilized active conformation, and may also improve agonist potency by stabilizing extracellular loop 2. Together, these findings establish the structural framework for cooperative multisite allostery in a GPCR, revealing how distributed allosteric sites act in concert to amplify receptor activation and providing a conceptual foundation for developing innovative GPCR allosteric therapeutics.

papers.abstract: We consider a two-dimensional wave system containing a subwavelength hole, such as an aperture in an interface supporting surface electromagnetic or acoustic waves or an island in a fluid surface sustaining gravity-capillary waves. Recent studies have revealed the emergence of pronounced wave vortices around such structures, termed type II vortices, in contrast to conventional (type I) vortices associated with phase singularities and intensity nulls. A notable natural manifestation of type II vortices occurs in ocean tides around islands such as New Zealand, Madagascar, and Iceland, where the tidal phase increases by ±2π around the island. Although this phenomenon is usually associated with the Coriolis effect from the rotation of the Earth, here, we demonstrate the controlled generation of type II vortices using a minimal and tunable setup: a dipole-oscillating subwavelength hole and a single incident plane wave. Using laboratory gravity-capillary waves and an oscillating subwavelength "island," we directly measure the resulting phase structure, topological charge, and wave angular momentum. We show that the emergence and handedness of the vortices can be precisely controlled via the relative phase between the dipolar source and the incident wave. Our results offer a simple and versatile mechanism for engineering subwavelength wave vortices, with potential applications in a variety of two-dimensional wave systems.

papers.abstract: Retrospective studies in patients with nonmuscle invasive bladder cancer have reported a significant reduction in Alzheimer's disease incidence (12 to 78%) among Bacille Calmette-Guérin (BCG) recipients versus controls. To investigate the underlying mechanisms, we evaluated BCG in the PS19 mouse model of tauopathy. We found that BCG administration reduced hippocampal phospho-tau and microgliosis while preserving neuronal markers. In vivo volumetric T2-magnetic resonance Imaging (MRI) demonstrated attenuation of brain atrophy accompanied by increased glutamate-weighted chemical exchange saturation transfer-MRI signals. Functionally, BCG-treated mice showed improved performance in the novel object recognition test, as well as improved body-weight maintenance and survival. Transcriptomic profiling of the hippocampus revealed near complete normalization of the PS19 disease-associated gene expression signature toward that of healthy controls. Flow cytometric profiling of brain myeloid populations demonstrated a reduction in activated resident microglia, but total microglia cells remain elevated. Moreover, an increase of trained immunity marker CD80 on the recruited peripheral myeloid cells ensues following BCG treatment. Consistent with this shift in myeloid state, primary brain myeloid cells from BCG-treated mice also exhibited enhanced phagocytosis of fluorescein isothiocyanate-labeled tau fibrils and increased lactate production. Together, these findings indicate that BCG induces systemic and central nervous system myeloid cell reprogramming that limits neuroinflammation, enhances tau clearance, and rescues cognitive and neurodegenerative phenotypes in a tauopathy model. BCG is a safe, readily available therapy that merits consideration as a preventive agent against dementia.

papers.abstract: T cell exhaustion limits the success of cancer immunotherapies, yet the proteomic changes underlying this dysfunctional state remain poorly understood. We integrated transcriptomics, quantitative proteomics, turnover proteomics, and ubiquitin proteomics to construct a multi-omic atlas of T cell exhaustion. These studies identified pathways regulated through transcriptional and post-translational mechanisms, including degradative and nondegradative ubiquitin modifications, and uncovered widespread changes in proteostasis, metabolism, and DNA repair. Major shifts were revealed in the ubiquitin-proteasome system, as differential expression of E3 ubiquitin ligases correlates with immunotherapy outcomes. These findings position the collapse of proteostasis as a central, underappreciated feature of T cell exhaustion and reveal opportunities to restore T cell function. We demonstrate that overexpression of the E3 ligase RNF166 enhances T cell persistence in vitro and in vivo. This work defines proteome-turnover dynamics as a critical regulatory layer in progressive T cell dysfunction, with broad implications for advancing cancer immunotherapy through manipulation of E3 ligases.

papers.abstract: Cell Painting is a popular high-content imaging assay that captures the shape and internal organization of 2D cell cultures at scale. While 3D cell cultures are more physiologically relevant models - especially for studying drug perturbations - they remain challenging to image because light scatters before it reaches the cultures' interior. Here, we introduce a scalable method to adapt Cell Painting for 3D spheroids. We show that tissue-clearing, a technique that makes spheroids transparent, combined with a focusing routine that locates spheroids on the fly, enables Cell Painting at single-cell level inside intact spheroids. By profiling 52 clinically relevant drugs, we show that single-cell fingerprints clustered by biological pathway and resolved drug effects more robustly than those of flattened spheroid-wide views. Notably, the effect of two drugs, 5-fluorouracil and olaparib, nearly indistinguishable in 2D monolayers, diverged in spheroids. This finding was then corroborated by DNA-damage, cell-cycle, and gene-expression assays. The workflow runs on a spinning-disk confocal microscope in a standard 384-well plate format, making single-cell 3D profiling accessible to laboratories already performing Cell Painting.

papers.abstract: The organization of signaling proteins into multi-component complexes is essential for innate immune responses and is often achieved through the oligomerization of death domains (DDs). The Myddosome, composed of MyD88 and IRAK family kinases, exemplifies this mechanism. However, how DDs assemble in an ordered and regulated manner to form Myddosomes to control signaling output remains unclear. Here, we show that IRAK4 kinase activity and autophosphorylation are required for IRAK4:IRAK1 heterotypic DD interactions. We show that IRAK1 is autoinhibited by its kinase domain, and IRAK4 phosphorylation relieves this inhibition, enabling IRAK1 DD incorporation into Myddosomes. This phosphorylation-dependent switch similarly controls IRAK2/3 incorporation. Thus, IRAK4 autophosphorylation acts as an energy-dependent molecular switch that integrates phosphorylation with protein oligomerization to drive Myddosome maturation and signal transduction. This mechanism demonstrates how enzymatic activity can impose temporal and spatial control over macromolecular assembly to ensure directional and context-dependent inflammatory signaling.

papers.abstract: To evaluate correlations between pressure-based dynamic preload indices and echocardiographic flow velocity variations during coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). Prospective observational pilot study. Single university hospital. Thirty adults undergoing elective CABG. Modified passive leg raising (PLR) at 3 intraoperative time points. Mean arterial pressure increased after PLR at all 3 time points. In pooled analyses, stroke volume variation decreased from 13% ± 4% to 10% ± 4% and pulse pressure variation decreased from 10% ± 2% to 7% ± 3% (both p < 0.05). Respiratory peak velocity variations in the left ventricular outflow tract and descending aorta did not change significantly. Pulse contour-derived cardiac output also did not change (5.1 ± 1.1 L/min v 5.1 ± 1.1 L/min, p = 0.71). Stroke volume variation and pulse pressure variation correlated strongly (r = 0.720), whereas correlations between pressure- and flow-derived indices were weak (r = 0.147-0.351). Pressure-derived indices correlated only weakly with echocardiographic respiratory peak velocity variations in patients undergoing CABG. As forward flow did not measurably increase following modified PLR, the physiological significance of these weak correlations remains uncertain.

papers.abstract: Homologous recombination deficiency (HRD) is a critical biomarker for guiding treatment decisions in high-grade serous tubo-ovarian carcinoma (HGSOC), a cancer with few reliable biomarkers. However, existing genomics-based tests for HRD are variable, expensive, and time-consuming. We develop HRDPath, a patient-level deep learning architecture that predicts HRD status from whole slide images, requiring no additional molecular testing. HRDPath is validated across three cohorts of female patients and achieves an AUC of 0.846, significantly outperforming previously reported results in HGSOC. By incorporating multiple slides per patient and targeted optimization strategies, we strengthen the model clinical utility, with both specificity and sensitivity reaching 0.90. Our interpretability pipeline enhances model trustworthiness and reveals important clinical and biological insights into HRD-positive cancers, highlighting the associated morphological and pathological changes at the cellular and tissue levels. HRDPath provides a foundation for an accessible and scalable digital biomarker to improve treatment stratification in ovarian cancer globally.

papers.abstract: Plant development is highly plastic, with growth and architecture continuously shaped by environmental conditions. Roots, for instance, adjust their development to local water, nutrient and soil conditions. Despite this plasticity, individual root cell types are generally viewed as largely homogeneous populations that progress along a single developmental trajectory1. Here we show that rather than progressing along a single developmental trajectory, most Arabidopsis root cell lineage trajectories exhibit a stereotyped bifid topology, as revealed by single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcript mapping. One branch is characterized by a transcriptional program that is shared across multiple cell types and enriched for genes associated with environmental responses, including abscisic acid (ABA) signalling. This state occurs reproducibly in a subset of cells across multiple cell types, independent of developmental lineage, thereby revealing an additional layer of root cell identity. It is conserved across Arabidopsis ecotypes and persists despite major perturbations in developmental identity. Moreover, it is reduced in ABA-deficient and ABA-insensitive mutants and becomes more prevalent under water-deficit conditions. Together, these findings reveal an additional layer of root cell identity that is superimposed on developmental lineage and its prevalence is modulated by environmental conditions. These results uncover a previously unrecognized source of environment-associated transcriptional heterogeneity shared across root cell types.

papers.abstract: Hantaviruses are rodent-borne pathogens that cause severe human disease for which no approved therapeutics are available. New World hantaviruses, including Andes virus (ANDV), use the cell-surface receptor protocadherin-1 (PCDH1) to enter host cells1. However, the structural basis of this interaction remains unclear. Here we describe the structure of PCDH1 bound to the ANDV spike at near-atomic resolution. PCDH1 asymmetrically engages a deep central pocket formed by four Gn protomers in the spike, explaining why only intact viral particles or soluble tetramers recognize it. Mutagenesis identified three Gn loops that shape the receptor-binding site and afford the transfer of PCDH1 binding from New World to Old World glycoproteins. Structural and functional analyses of four neutralizing antibodies revealed that they block receptor binding through two distinct mechanisms-occluding access to the PCDH1-binding site or sterically preventing receptor engagement. Together, these findings define the structural determinants of hantavirus-receptor recognition, reveal how a virus can mask its receptor-binding site by recessing it in a surface depression and how antibodies can counter this strategy, and provide a framework for the design of antiviral therapeutics targeting the hantavirus spike.

papers.abstract: Mitochondria are bound by a double membrane and are semiautonomous organelles, rendering them highly vulnerable to global and internal proteostatic stress1. Multiple surveillance mechanisms at proteostatic and inter-organellar levels have evolved to maintain mitochondrial integrity and cellular health2-7. However, the precise mechanisms by which proteostatic damage relays stress signals across organelles and how the quality surveillance machinery coordinates these functions remain unknown. Here we report that under proteostatic stress, damaged mitochondrial proteins are sequestered to form stress-induced mitochondrial protein aggregates (SIMPAs) that activate specific quality control mechanisms in a spatially confined manner without perturbing the mitochondrial network. Quantitative proteomic and correlative light-electron microscopy analysis revealed that SIMPA mediates inter-organellar communication via mitochondria-endoplasmic reticulum contact sites or mitochondrial-associated membranes. Mechanistically, GRP75 coordinates SIMPA biogenesis and focally activates endoplasmic reticulum unfolded protein response pathways via mitochondria-endoplasmic reticulum contact sites or mitochondrial-associated membranes for the targeted clearance of SIMPAs. Functionally, in both cellular and liver disease models, we found that a GRP75-dependent SIMPA signalling cascade attenuates mitochondrial stress and preserves mitochondrial integrity under proteotoxic stress. Overall, we show that SIMPAs, functioning as protein condensates, serve as a central cross-compartment communication hub for mitochondrial quality control, supporting cellular and organismal fitness.

papers.abstract: Moderately cold temperatures extend lifespan and promote health across species1-3, yet the molecular mechanisms underlying these benefits remain unclear. Here we define a metabolite-driven, multi-tissue signalling system that links cold temperature to enhanced longevity and proteostasis in Caenorhabditis elegans. Cold temperature upregulates the biopterin-synthesis enzyme CAT-4 (GCH1 in humans), increasing production of dihydrobiopterin (BH2), a transportable reservoir for the bioactive cofactor tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4). BH2 is produced in muscle and transported to distal tissues, including the intestine and neurons, where it is converted into BH4 by the salvage enzyme DHFR-1. BH4 functions as an essential cofactor for phenylalanine hydroxylase PAH-1, promoting tyrosine synthesis and extending lifespan. This BH2-BH4 axis also prevents disease-related protein aggregation and subsequent neuronal dysfunction during ageing. Importantly, increasing BH2 synthesis specifically in muscle is sufficient to promote longevity and suppress pathological protein aggregation in distal tissues, even at normal or elevated temperatures. In human cells, BH2 or tyrosine supplementation reduces aggregation of polyQ-expanded proteins associated with Huntington's disease, as well as mutant variants of TDP-43 and FUS that cause amyotrophic lateral sclerosis. Together, these findings identify BH2 as a cold-induced metabolite of which the synthesis, intertissue transport and conversion into bioactive BH4 preserve organism-wide proteostasis and extend lifespan.

papers.abstract: Angelman syndrome is a severe neurodevelopmental disorder caused by the loss of UBE3A, a gene that encodes an E3 ubiquitin ligase1,2. The mechanisms that underlie Angelman syndrome are not well understood, and in particular, the link between UBE3A substrates and disease phenotypes remains uncertain3. Here, using gain- and loss-of-function mutations in UBE3A4,5 along with unbiased proteomics, we show that asparagine synthetase (ASNS) is a target of UBE3A. We find that ASNS protein abundance is increased in the brains of Ube3a-null mice and in human neurons6. Genetic correction of ASNS overabundance rescues microcephaly and many behavioural deficits. Detailed molecular analyses show that ASNS overabundance activates stress signalling and causes a global reduction in neuronal protein synthesis. Our results suggest that loss of UBE3A traps neurons in a state of persistent stress and stunts neuronal growth during developmentally sensitive periods. Moreover, our results indicate that targeting ASNS and the stress response could hold therapeutic potential in Angelman syndrome.

papers.abstract: Magnetic tunnel junctions based on ferromagnets are canonical devices in spintronics, with wide-ranging applications in data storage, computing and sensing. They simultaneously exhibit mechanisms for electrical detection and control of magnetic order through the tunnelling magnetoresistance (TMR)1-5 and spin-transfer torque6-9 effects, respectively. It was long assumed that neither of these effects could be sizeable in all-antiferromagnetic tunnel junctions (AATJs), considering that they have no net magnetization. However, it was recently shown that AATJs based on chiral antiferromagnets do exhibit TMR due to their non-relativistic momentum-dependent spin polarization and cluster magnetic octupole moment, which are manifestations of their spin-split band structure10-13. However, the reciprocal effect, that is, the antiferromagnetic counterpart of spin-transfer torque, has been assumed non-existent due to the total electric current being spin-neutral. Here we report nanoscale AATJs that display this reciprocal effect, which we term octupole-driven spin-transfer torque (OTT). We demonstrate current-induced OTT switching of PtMn3|MgO|PtMn3 AATJs, with a TMR value of 363% at room temperature and switching current densities of the order of 10 MA cm-2. Our theoretical modelling explains the origin of OTT in terms of the imbalance between intra- and inter-sublattice spin currents across the AATJ, and, equivalently, in terms of the non-zero net cluster octupole polarization of each PtMn3 layer. This work establishes a new materials platform for antiferromagnetic spintronics and provides a pathway towards deeply scaled magnetic memory and room-temperature terahertz technologies.

papers.abstract: Dietary fibers modulate host-microbiota interactions. Whether fiber promotes epithelial repair through microbiota-dependent mechanisms remains unclear. We determined how alginate influences colitis recovery and whether the pathway is relevant to ulcerative colitis (UC). We screened fibers in dextran sodium sulfate (DSS)-induced murine colitis and assessed survival, inflammation, barrier function, and epithelial regeneration. Microbiota dependence was evaluated using antibiotics and bacterial supplementation. Metabolites were profiled using capillary electrophoresis-time-of-flight mass spectrometry (CE-TOFMS), and epithelial programs were analyzed using RNA-seq and colonic organoid injury assays. Slc6a6-/- and Cyp2c55-/- mice were used to determine mechanistic requirements. Translational relevance was examined in a randomized, placebo-controlled trial of UC patients receiving antibiotic-primed fecal microbiota transplantation (A-FMT) followed by alginate or placebo. Clinical outcomes, histology, fecal taurine, and colonic CYP2C18 expression were assessed. Alginate improved DSS colitis recovery, reducing inflammation, restoring barrier integrity, and enhancing crypt proliferation. Alginate enriched taurine-releasing bacteria, including Bacteroides acidifaciens and Ligilactobacillus murinus, and increased intestinal taurine; antibiotic disruption abrogated these effects. Taurine was required for benefit, as alginate failed in Slc6a6-/- mice. Alginate and taurine induced epithelial Cyp2c55, and protection was lost in Cyp2c55-/- mice and organoids. In the clinical trial, the primary endpoint was not met. However, alginate supplementation was associated with biological changes, including fecal taurine levels and colonic CYP2C18 expression, consistent with preclinical mechanisms. Alginate engages a fiber-microbiota-taurine-epithelial signaling pathway that promotes recovery in preclinical models. The clinical trial did not meet its primary endpoint; however, the biological changes warrant further investigation of alginate as a microbiota-targeted intervention. jRCTs031200103 (https://jrct.mhlw.go.jp/), registered September 1, 2020: UMIN000041968 (https://www.umin.ac.jp/ctr/index.htm), October 1, 2020.

papers.abstract: Metabolic dysregulation in obesity reshapes immune function, but how lipid signals drive immune suppression remains unclear. Herein, we identify a FABP4-PD-L1 axis that links lipid metabolism to immune checkpoint regulation in myeloid cells. Single-cell transcriptomics revealed a distinct FABP4high immunosuppressive splenic macrophage subset enriched under high-fat diet (HFD) conditions, characterized by impaired antigen presentation and elevated PD-L1 expression. Mechanistically, palmitic acid (PA) was shown to induce FABP4 and promote PD-L1 palmitoylation, leading to its stabilization on the cell surface independent of transcriptional regulation. FABP4 was essential for this process, which enabled PD-L1 surface stabilization, immunosuppression and mammary tumor progression. In humans, a conserved CD14intCD16⁺ monocyte population exhibited elevated FABP4-PD-L1 signaling and correlated with obesity and invasive breast cancer. These findings establish PD-L1 as a metabolically regulated protein and reveal a mechanism by which lipid excess drives immune evasion, suggesting FABP4 as a potential therapeutic target in cancer immunotherapy.

papers.abstract: Cerebral computed tomography angiography (CTA) is increasingly incorporated into national guidelines to confirm cerebral circulatory arrest during the determination of death using neurological criteria. However, implementation remains limited due to studies showing variable sensitivity. Clinical observations suggest the time elapsed from the onset of initial signs of brainstem areflexia, defined as the appearance of fixed and dilated pupils and loss of cough and gag reflexes, significantly influences CTA sensitivity. This study aimed to evaluate the impact of this time interval on test sensitivity. We retrospectively assessed 118 intensive care unit patients undergoing determination of death using neurological criteria. Cerebral CTA was used to confirm cerebral circulatory arrest based on a four-point scoring system. Patients were categorised according to the time elapsed from the onset of initial signs of brainstem areflexia to the investigation. Cerebral CTA did not confirm cerebral circulatory arrest in 15/118 (13%) patients, yielding an overall sensitivity of 87.3% (95%CI 79.6-92.5%). Notably, 93.3% (95%CI 66.0-99.7%) of false-negative results occurred within 12 h of the onset of initial signs of brainstem areflexia. Patients were secondarily stratified into early (≤ 12 h) and late (> 12 h) groups, revealing a significantly higher sensitivity in the late group (67.4%, 95%CI 51.3-80.5% vs. 98.7%, 95%CI 91.8-100%, p < 0.001). The sensitivity of cerebral CTA increases with the time elapsed after the onset of initial signs of brainstem areflexia. We recommend delaying cerebral CTA until at least 12 h after the onset of initial signs of brainstem areflexia, and, in case of inconclusive results, test repetition at least 12 h later. Further work is required to confirm our findings and increase diagnostic confidence.

papers.abstract: The supraglottic airway device i-gelTM Plus (Intersurgical Ltd., Berkshire, UK) may provide more secure ventilation than the original i-gelTM (Intersurgical Ltd., Berkshire, UK). This prospective randomized trial was conducted to evaluate the performance of i-gelTM Plus compared with the original i-gelTM in patients in the lateral decubitus position under general anesthesia with a neuromuscular blocking drug. We inserted two types of i-gelTM in the supine position in adult patients undergoing general anesthesia with 0.6 mg/kg IV rocuronium. The primary outcome was oropharyngeal leak pressure in the lateral position. Secondary outcomes included expiratory tidal volume and glottic view in that position. We analyzed 84 surgical patients in the i-gelTM Plus [n = 42] and original i-gelTM [n = 42] groups. The oropharyngeal leak pressure and expiratory tidal volume at the oropharyngeal leak pressure in the supine position were similar between the two groups. The lateral decubitus position demonstrated higher oropharyngeal leak pressure (P < 0.001) and expiratory tidal volume at oropharyngeal leak pressure (P < 0.001) in the i-gelTM Plus group (median [interquartile range], 22 [20-25] cmH2O and 694 [602-750] ml, respectively) than in the original i-gelTM group (15 [14-18] cmH2O and 470 [420-634] ml, respectively). However, fiberoptic glottis view grade scores did not differ between the two groups. The i-gelTM Plus implements higher oropharyngeal leak pressure in the lateral decubitus position than the original i-gelTM. Our results indicate that the i-gelTM Plus may be a better choice as a supraglottic airway device in the lateral decubitus position than the original i-gelTM in paralyzed patients. papers.abstract: Pre-emptive antibiotic therapy is frequently prescribed after pancreaticoduodenectomy when intraoperative bile cultures are positive, despite the absence of clinical infection. Evidence supporting this practice remains limited. We assessed the association between withholding pre-emptive antibiotics and postoperative outcomes in patients with biliary colonization. This multicenter retrospective cohort study included 301 consecutive adults undergoing pancreaticoduodenectomy with positive intraoperative bile cultures in four French tertiary centers between January 2014 and December 2024. Overall, 89 patients received PE-ATB, and 212 did not. Propensity score matching at a 1:2 ratio yielded 138 patients, including 46 treated patients and 92 controls. The primary outcome was 5-year overall survival. Secondary postoperative outcomes were examined using prespecified exploratory non-inferiority margins. Preoperative biliary stenting independently predicted PE-ATB use (odds ratio, 4.11; 95% confidence interval, 1.26-13.40;P = 0.019). In the matched cohort, withholding PE-ATB was compatible with the non-inferiority margin for intra-abdominal abscess, pancreatic fistula, transfusion requirements, and antibiotic duration. Overall postoperative infection did not differ significantly between groups (odds ratio, 1.42; 95% confidence interval, 0.66-3.07; P = 0.376). Five-year mortality was higher in the group without PE-ATB in the matched cohort (hazard ratio, 2.02; 95% confidence interval, 1.01-4.04; P = 0.048), whereas no survival difference was observed in the overall unmatched cohort. Withholding PE-ATB was not associated with worse early postoperative outcomes and was associated with reduced antibiotic exposure. The survival difference observed only after matching should be considered cautiously and may reflect residual confounding. Prospective randomized trials are needed.

papers.abstract: Some parturients experience discomfort, pain, and nausea/vomiting during cesarean delivery under neuraxial anesthesia. We evaluated whether intravenous dexmedetomidine administered after fetal delivery and cord clamping improved maternal intraoperative experience. In this prospective, triple-blind, placebo-controlled trial, women aged 20-45 years undergoing elective cesarean delivery under combined spinal-epidural anesthesia were randomized 1:1 to dexmedetomidine or saline. Dexmedetomidine was administered after cord clamping as a loading dose of 1 μg/kg over 10 min, followed by 0.4 μg/kg/hr until peritoneal closure; controls received equivalent-volume saline. The primary outcome was satisfaction with intraoperative sedation/analgesia, assessed on postoperative day 1 using a 7-point verbal rating scale. Secondary outcomes were Quality of Recovery-40 score, maximum intraoperative pain score, intraoperative nausea/vomiting, and motor recovery time. Eighty-three participants were randomized; 81 contributed to the available-case analysis. Satisfaction scores were higher with dexmedetomidine than saline (Hodges-Lehmann location shift, 1.0 point; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.0 to 2.0; P < 0.001). In ordinal logistic regression, dexmedetomidine was associated with higher satisfaction scores (common odds ratio, 13.4; 95% CI 4.6 to 39.0). Dexmedetomidine reduced intraoperative pain and intraoperative nausea/vomiting, but did not improve 24-h Quality of Recovery-40 scores and modestly prolonged motor recovery. Post-delivery intravenous dexmedetomidine improved patient-reported satisfaction with intraoperative sedation and analgesia. Exploratory findings suggested reduced pain and nausea/vomiting without improved 24-h recovery. These findings support further evaluation of dexmedetomidine as a selective adjunct rather than for routine sedation. papers.abstract: The tumour immune microenvironment influences neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy success in esophageal adenocarcinoma (EAC). Complete responders show higher treatment-naïve intratumoral CD8+ T cell levels before treatment than non-complete responders. Understanding mechanisms driving CD8+ T cells exclusion from the TIME is essential to improving outcomes. We performed spatial transcriptomics on treatment-naive CD8-low and high EACs (N = 12). Regions of interest (ROIs) were selected based on tumour annotation by a pathologist. Cancer (CK+) cells and immune (CD45+) cells were analysed within the same ROI. Findings were validated using bulk transcriptome data (TCGA) and metabolic profiling (SCENITH) of fresh tumour specimen (n = 5). Whole transcriptomic profiling showed cancer cell clustering based on T cell infiltration. Cancer cell transcriptomes of CD8-low tumours exhibited reduced antigen presentation and upregulated lipid and mitochondrial metabolism, while CD8-high tumours showed increased cytokine signalling and apoptotic pathways. In CD45+ compartments, CD8-low tumours were enriched for the PGC-1α pathway, linked to mitochondrial biogenesis and immunosuppressive myeloid populations. These findings were supported by TCGA data. SCENITH confirmed mitochondrial dependence of macrophages in CD8-low tumours. Our results suggest that mitochondrial metabolism and impaired antigen presentation contribute to T cell exclusion in EAC. These findings raise the hypothesis that targeting mitochondrial metabolism in these cancers can modulate the anti-tumour immune response and thereby improve the response to chemoradiotherapy.

papers.abstract: WEE1 phosphorylates and inhibits the activity of cyclin-dependent kinases to prevent mitotic entry and establish a G2 DNA damage checkpoint1-3. Consequently, WEE1 inhibitors have been developed to be synthetically lethal in TP53-mutated tumours that become reliant on this WEE1-mediated checkpoint, and such inhibitors are undergoing clinical trials. However, WEE1 inhibitors also have efficacy in TP53-wild-type tumours, and many trials have been terminated owing to high levels of toxic side effects, suggesting that WEE1 has unknown functions. Here we show that WEE1 promotes cell cycle re-entry from quiescence (G0) by opposing the activity of the E3 ubiquitin ligase, anaphase-promoting complex-cyclosome bound to CDH1 (APC/CCDH1). WEE1 phosphorylates CDH1 (FZR1) at key residues that mediate the interaction between CDH1 and APC/C. Cells with loss of function of WEE1 during G0/G1 have delayed S phase entry, impaired G1/S transition, abnormal S phase accumulation of cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitor p21Cip1/Kip1 and a p21-dependent G2 arrest. Reduced expression of APC/CCDH1 or p21 renders cells more sensitive to acute WEE1 inhibition, and both pathways are downregulated in cells with acquired WEE1 inhibitor resistance. These results reveal a mechanism of cell cycle control that has implications for how WEE1 inhibitors should be used in the clinic.

papers.abstract: Digital twin models can accelerate therapeutic development by enabling low-risk testing of candidate interventions. In preterm labor (PTL), a major pregnancy complication where clinical trials face ethical and financial barriers, digital twins are especially valuable for evaluating new therapies targeting immune dysfunctions driving PTL. Yet, current models lack single-cell resolution, limiting detection of cell type-specific mechanisms, off-target effects, and the design of personalized interventions. We present Simulated Immunome Modeling of Clinical Outcomes (SIMCO), a single-cell-level digital twin framework that models immunomodulatory treatment effects on the timing of labor using immunome-wide, single-cell simulations. SIMCO's digital twins are trained and validated on a newly generated mass cytometry atlas of the pregnant immunome exposed to nine candidate drugs preselected for PTL prevention. Applying SIMCO to an independent cohort of pregnant individuals, we simulate treatment effects on gestational length, screening for candidate drugs that delay labor timing and providing system-level mechanistic insight for each drug candidate. Tetrahydrofolate and the combination of aspirin and lansoprazole emerged as top candidates for PTL prevention, delaying labor onset primarily through enhanced mTOR signaling in innate immune cells and attenuated JAK/STAT signaling in naïve CD4+ T cells.

papers.abstract: This meta-analysis aimed to evaluate whether intraoperative hemoadsorption during cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) improves postoperative outcomes compared with the standard of care. We systematically searched EMBASE, PubMed, and the Cochrane Library for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing hemoadsorption versus standard care in patients undergoing cardiac surgery with CPB. Data were analyzed using a frequentist approach and trial sequential analysis (TSA). The primary outcome was the incidence of cardiac surgery-associated acute kidney injury (CSA-AKI) within 7 days after surgery. The protocol was prospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD42025634991). A total of six RCTs comprising 798 patients were included. Four RCTs (n = 723; 355 hemoadsorption, 368 control) reported CSA-AKI incidence, which did not significantly differ between groups (RR = 0.93 [95% CI: 0.71-1.21], p = 0.57; I² = 42.0%). Hemoadsorption was not associated with significant differences in secondary outcomes: interleukin-6, tumor necrosis factor, 28-day mortality, SOFA score, and ICU length of stay. Hemoadsorption during CPB was not associated with a reduction in CSA-AKI or with improvement in secondary clinical outcomes in elective patients undergoing cardiac surgery. However, the accrued sample represented only 48% of the heterogeneity-adjusted required information size (1,491 patients), and the cumulative Z-curve crossed neither the monitoring nor the futility boundary. papers.abstract: Breast cancer develops within spatially organized, multicellular microenvironments in which particular tumor-associated macrophage (TAM) states can influence immune access and stromal remodeling. Conventional M1/M2 classification and total macrophage density fail to capture the developmental, transcriptional, metabolic, and spatial heterogeneity that determines TAM function. This macrophage-focused review examines breast cancer within its multicellular microenvironment, integrating lineage-tracing, single-cell, spatial, mechanistic, and clinical evidence while distinguishing breast-specific findings from hypotheses extrapolated from other tumors. We examine how tissue-resident and monocyte-derived macrophages are recruited, retained, expanded, and reprogrammed across primary and metastatic sites, emphasizing interactions with malignant cells, cancer-associated fibroblasts, extracellular matrix, vasculature, adipose tissue, and lymphoid populations. In defined breast-tumor contexts, TAM programs have been implicated in immune exclusion, invasion, metastatic dissemination, and adaptation to systemic treatment, although evidence strength varies across mechanisms and therapeutic modalities. Small and heterogeneous clinical studies have not established a benefit from broad CSF1/CSF1R-axis targeting in breast cancer, despite encouraging preclinical findings. Accordingly, we highlight a shift toward state-selective, spatially resolved, and temporally coordinated targeting. Emerging approaches include restoring phagocytosis, disrupting chemokine and fibrotic circuits, metabolic reprogramming, and converting suppressive TAMs into inflammatory, antigen-presenting effectors. A major focus is chimeric antigen receptor macrophage (CAR-M) therapy, which combines antigen-directed phagocytosis with tumor infiltration, matrix remodeling, antigen presentation, and recruitment of endogenous immunity. Although early clinical data support manufacturing feasibility, tumor trafficking, and acceptable initial safety, limited antitumor activity underscores challenges involving antigen heterogeneity, persistence, metabolic fitness, biodistribution, and scalable production. We propose a translational roadmap integrating spatial biomarkers, quantitative target selection, macrophage-adapted CAR design, checkpoint-resistant phagocytosis, metabolic engineering, safety switches, and biomarker-guided combination therapy. This framework positions macrophage reprogramming as a context-dependent strategy for modifying selected breast-tumor niches, with therapeutic targets chosen according to the macrophage program and its surrounding cellular architecture.
